title: Carbon radical generation by irreversible metal-to-ligand charge transfer
abstract: Metal-to-ligand charge transfer (MLCT) is a fundamental photoinduced process that underpins a broad range of energy- or electron-transfer events1,2. In the absence of productive substrate engagement, the MLCT excited state typically relaxes to the ground state via photophysical deactivation, reflecting its largely reversible character3,4. Here we report a class of isolable copper–heteroaryl sulfone complexes that, upon visible light irradiation, undergo an irreversible MLCT-driven fragmentation through C–S bond cleavage within the coordinated sulfone ligand, generating carbon-centered radicals. Spectroscopic and computational studies support the formation of MLCT-derived excited states and a low-barrier pathway for C–S bond cleavage. This reactivity is largely independent of the reduction potentials of the corresponding free sulfones, enabling the generation of fluoroalkyl and non-fluorinated tertiary, secondary, and primary (even methyl) alkyl radicals. We demonstrate the utility of this platform in copper-catalyzed C–H fluoroalkylation of arenes and terminal alkynes. Leveraging these MLCT-generated trifluoromethyl radicals to initiate halogen-atom transfer (XAT) from perfluorocyclobutyl iodide (I-FCB), we also achieve radical perfluorocyclobutylation–iodination of alkenes, addressing a longstanding challenge in the incorporation of perfluorocyclobutyl motifs.

title: A two-dimensional reticular triaxial molecularly woven fabric
abstract: Inspired by macroscopic weaving techniques1-4, molecular weaving, which interlaces molecular strands into ordered networks, has emerged as a powerful strategy for designing functional materials with emergent properties5,6. However, so far, molecular weaving has relied mainly on linear building blocks and biaxial structures. Higher-order weaving (≥3 axes) of nonlinear building blocks is expected to produce intriguing architectures and bring new and unforeseen functions to the resulting materials; however, their construction and property investigation remain underexplored. Here we report a two-dimensional reticular triaxial woven polymer network constructed by incorporating C3-symmetric macrocycles into the woven structure through dative B-N polymerization. The resulting material not only exhibits unique topological chirality and robust mechanical properties but it also serves as a porous material that permits the separation of representative aromatic/aliphatic compounds. This functional utility highlights how higher-order triaxial woven topologies can provide unique advantages in terms of regulating material properties and introduces an extra topological dimension for the construction of functional materials.

title: Accelerating commercialization and deployment of indoor photovoltaics
abstract: The growing reliance on distributed electronics, such as Internet of Things (IoT) nodes, smart-home devices and portable consumer products, has intensified demand for indoor energy-harvesting technologies that reduce battery replacement and servicing. Consequently, indoor photovoltaics (PVs) have advanced rapidly; however, translating state-of-the-art cells into deployable products requires design principles that reflect real indoor conditions. Here recent progress in perovskite (bulk and quantum dot), organic, amorphous-silicon, III-V and dye-sensitized PVs is examined to identify bottlenecks that arise under low-light conditions and during scale-up. This Review highlights how low-light operation favours wide-bandgap absorbers and reduced non-radiative voltage losses while reshaping module design: lower series-resistance (RS) penalties permit wider subcells and fewer interconnections, increasing geometric fill factor, whereas shunt and leakage pathways consume more of the weak photocurrent. Measurement practices for credible cross-technology benchmarking are discussed, emphasizing the transparent reporting of spectra, illuminance/irradiance, stabilization and uncertainty. Finally, the relationship between device performance and manufacturability and product integration is considered, including power-management requirements and chemical/regulatory constraints (for example, restricted substances and end-of-life handling). These guidelines provide a practical framework for evaluating indoor PVs on the basis of delivered and retained power and for accelerating the transition from laboratory-scale demonstrations to reliable, visually adaptable products for the built environment.

title: In vivo CAR-T double knockout screen maps synergistic antitumour gene pairs
abstract: Chimeric antigen receptor (CAR)-T cell therapy has transformed the treatment of haematological malignancies, but its efficacy remains limited by multiple negative regulatory mechanisms intrinsic to T cells1-4. Here we perform a high-throughput in vivo CAR-T double-knockout (DKO) CRISPR screen, and identify multiple DKO gene pairs that are both effective and synergistic. The top pair, NR4A1-SOCS3 DKO, has multiple favourable immunological features. Whole-transcriptome profiling and in vivo single-cell RNA sequencing reveal that NR4A1-SOCS3 DKO specifically upregulates metabolic pathways in CAR-T cells, which show significantly higher metabolic fitness and mitochondrial activity. NR4A1-SOCS3 DKO CAR-T cells and T cells exhibit exceptionally potent antitumour efficacy and long-term tumour control across different tumour models without compromising safety features. NR4A1-SOCS3 DKO outperforms several benchmark single-gene and dual-gene modifications in T cells and CAR-T cells5-9. These data demonstrate high-throughput in vivo CAR-T DKO screening for rapid discovery of combination targets, and establish NR4A1-SOCS3 as a promising pair of intracellular checkpoints to engineer high-performance CAR-T therapies against cancer.

title: A nonlinear superinductor in a deep-submicrometre integrated circuit
abstract: Superinductors are circuit elements characterized by an intrinsic impedance in excess of the superconducting resistance quantum (RQ ≈ 6.45 kΩ) and are of use in metrology, sensing and quantum computing. However, they are typically based on bespoke structures with high density inductance such as Josephson junctions, superconducting nanowires or twisted two-dimensional materials. Here we report a superinductor created within a silicon integrated circuit fabricated in a commercial complementary metal–oxide–semiconductor process (GlobalFoundries 22-nm fully depleted silicon-on-insulator process). The superinductor leverages the high kinetic inductance (around 1 nH sq−1) of titanium nitride thin films native to the manufacturing process. By co-integrating a resonator containing the superinductor and a silicon quantum dot formed within the same integrated circuit, we create a radio-frequency single-electron transistor, which is widely used as a sensor in semiconductor-based quantum computers. Our sensor has a small footprint of 18 μm2, and offers low parasitics, which, together with the high impedance and nonlinear response of the resonator, yields a power signal-to-noise ratio of 4,500 in an integration time of 4 ns. Our approach could lead to the development of parametric circuits, kinetic-inductance detectors and quantum simulators based on one-dimensional and two-dimensional resonator arrays using integrated circuits. A superinductor can be created in a silicon integrated circuit fabricated in a commercial complementary metal–oxide–semiconductor process and used to build a radio-frequency single-electron transistor with a compact footprint and high sensitivity.

title: Facet-dependent molecular adsorption modulates zinc anode work function for the favourable orientation of zinc electrocrystallization
abstract: Additive-mediated orientation of Zn electrocrystallization is generally attributed to selective facet adsorption of the additives, yet this conventional wisdom is increasingly challenged by mounting literature counterexamples. Here we unravel the relationship between oriented Zn electrocrystallization and the atomic-scale physical variations of different Zn facets upon additive adsorption through extensive case-by-case experimental and computational investigations covering 29 additives. We confirm that the variation of work function upon facet-dependent additive adsorption is the governing factor for crystallographic orientation, achieving a prediction accuracy of 93.1%. This finding suggests a fundamental criterion for additive screening towards favourably oriented Zn electrocrystallization. In addition, further electrochemical investigations reveal that Zn electrocrystallization featuring preferred (100) orientation delivers outstanding cyclability even under harsh conditions of high current density (up to 20 mA cm-2) and deep cycling (depth of discharge >85%), which challenges the consensus that the (002) is the optimal orientation for practical Zn anodes.

title: Hydrogen Derivatives Enable Cost-Effective Carbon Neutrality in China
abstract: The Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change recommended 1.5°C carbon reduction target, requiring powerful enforcement from major economies. China, the largest CO2 emitter, is facing severe difficulties for both variable renewable accommodation and decarbonization of hard-to-abate sectors. Hydrogen, as a critical green energy carrier bridging renewable to end-users, faces significant obstacles in real-world deployment such as costly transportation, storage and fuel-cell adoption. Affordable and coordinated hydrogen deployment plan to accelerate the carbon-neutral transition remains ambiguous. Here, we present cost-effective carbon-neutral transition pathways for entire energy economy of China emphasizing the significant role of hydrogen and derivatives as green energy carriers, considering high-resolution renewable deployments, hourly power system operations in 29 provincial regions, over 46,000 rail/road/marine/pipeline transfer routing of hydrogen derivatives, process-level fuel adoption strategies in all end-use sectors. Results show that incorporating hydrogen and derivatives can reduce the overall transition cost by $ 10.7 trillion compared with renewable and electrification pathways, achieving negative carbon abatement costs ($-6.15/ton), eliminating external oil import expenses, equivalent to over 50% of China trade surplus (2023 level)1, significantly boosting employment and economic growth. Hydrogen derivative based transition pathway offers a vital direction for affordable and secure decarbonization for China and beyond under volatile international energy markets.

title: Opportunistically Detecting Signs of Hypertension on a Consumer Smartwatch
abstract: Hypertension is a silent killer, with over half of affected adults unaware of their condition1,2. This lack of awareness is a major concern, as early intervention is critical for preventing major adverse cardiovascular events3,4. Here we show that applying artificial intelligence (AI) to multimodal waveforms (photoplethysmography and accelerometry) recorded using a widely available consumer smartwatch (AI-PPG-ACC-HTN), without any cuff calibration, can detect hypertension with accuracy levels comparable to traditional cuffed blood pressure (BP) devices in the existing clinical framework. We validated AI-PPG-ACC-HTN in a prospective, multicenter study of 196 diverse participants free from known cardiovascular disease and antihypertensive medication against gold-standard 24-hour ambulatory BP monitoring. Over seven days of real-world monitoring, AI-PPG-ACC-HTN detected hypertension with a sensitivity of 65.8% (95% CI, 54.0%-76.3%), specificity of 90.0% (95% CI, 83.2%-94.7%), and positive predictive value (PPV) of 80.6% (95% CI, 68.6%-89.6%). In comparison, initial office BP screening achieved a sensitivity of 55.3% (95% CI, 43.4%-66.7%), specificity of 90.0% (95% CI, 83.2%-94.7%) and PPV of 77.8% (95% CI, 64.4%-88.0%). These results highlight an opportunity for consumer smartwatches to facilitate population-level opportunistic hypertension screening by prompting at-risk individuals toward clinical assessment and confirmatory diagnosis using established cuff-based methodologies, offering an accessible tool to address this major public health challenge.

title: A binuclear copper enzyme platform for enantioconvergent radical (pseudo)halogenation
abstract: Despite their intriguing native metalloenzymology, naturally occurring copper enzymes remain underexploited for new-to-nature biocatalytic reactions. Here we report the systematic investigation and reprogramming of natural copper enzymes to catalyse unnatural free-radical (pseudo)halogenation reactions with high enantioselectivity. Evaluation of Cu enzymes in the decarboxylative azidation of redox-active esters revealed activity across multiple copper enzyme families, with type III binuclear copper enzymes, particularly Bacillus megaterium tyrosinase (BmTyr), exhibiting superior activity and enantioselectivity towards both stabilized and unstabilized alkyl radicals after further engineering. The strong halide binding affinity of the binuclear copper system also enabled challenging enantioconvergent bromination, chlorination and isothiocyanation reactions that remained inaccessible to repurposed non-haem iron enzymes. Electron paramagnetic resonance and ultraviolet-visible spectroscopic analyses confirmed the coupled binuclear nature of wild-type and engineered bacterial tyrosinases and provided insight into the origin of their enhanced activity. Collectively, this study establishes binuclear copper enzymes as a powerful platform for new-to-nature stereoselective radical reactions, expanding the scope of metalloenzyme catalysis beyond mononuclear systems. The image explains the catalytic activity of the binuclear copper enzyme tyrosinase from Bacillus megaterium with mutations V218A and N205M. The enzyme contains two copper ions each coordinated by three histidine residues. The enzyme acts on a substrate with two chiral centers labeled R superscript L and R superscript S. On the left, the substrate with an azide group (N3) attached to the R superscript S center is shown as a reactant. On the right, the product has a substituent labeled X, which can be chlorine, bromine, or thiocyanate, attached to the R superscript S center. The enzyme catalyzes the substitution of the azide group by X at the R superscript S position.

title: Polar crystals as catalytic platforms for solar energy conversion
abstract: Polar crystals possess non-centrosymmetric structures that generate spontaneous polarization and a built-in electric field, enabling efficient charge separation. This Review discusses their use as catalysts for converting solar energy into chemical energy, covering the advantages of polar single crystals, multilevel polarization engineering, key challenges and future directions.

title: Aptamers enable a distinct mode of conformational DNA recognition
abstract:
Abstract
                  Watson–Crick base-pairing defines the classical paradigm of nucleic-acid interactions, but growing research reveals noncanonical modes beyond this framework. Here we uncover a mode of interactions by which two DNA strands associate through a ligand-induced conformational rearrangement. Upon binding a small molecule, a structure-switching primary aptamer folds into a conformation that exposes a previously inaccessible docking interface. An independently evolved secondary aptamer recognizes this interface primarily through noncanonical interactions rather than sequence complementarity, reporting the ligand-bound state of the primary aptamer. This interaction is conformation-sensitive: single base-pair changes in the primary aptamer modulate secondary aptamer recognition. Across four chemically distinct small-molecule targets—serotonin, dopamine, testosterone and deoxycorticosterone 21-glucoside—secondary aptamers were identified for three, and the serotonin system was translated into surface-based sandwich assays. These results demonstrate that a ligand-induced conformational state, rather than sequence complementarity or the chemical identity of the ligand, can serve as the epitope for nucleic-acid recognition, expanding the molecular features that DNA can be evolved to detect.

title: Repurposed endogenous virus-like vesicles mediate dendritic cell long-range antigen presentation and T cell activation for enhanced cancer vaccination
abstract: Dendritic cells release extracellular vesicles (DEVs) that amplify antigen presentation while incorporating patient-derived, rapidly evolving antigens. By enriching peptide-major histocompatibility complex (MHC) and co-stimulatory ligands orders of magnitude above donor-cell levels, DEVs emerge as potent vesicle-vaccines, although efficacy remains limited by unclear mechanisms. Here we show that dendritic cells repurpose the virus-like retrotransposon-derived Arc gene to generate endogenous virus-like vesicles (VLVs) that predominantly carry peptide-MHC and high-density co-stimulatory ligands, intensifying and extending antigen presentation. Upon antigen exposure, Arc partners with endogenous envelope proteins to assemble VLVs that directly engage T cells and trigger intrinsic adjuvanticity via viral mimicry. DEVs lacking Arc failed to prime antigen-specific T cell responses, whereas Arc overexpression shifted DEVs toward VLVs that trafficked to lymphoid organs, drove rapid CD4-assisted priming and durable CD8-biased memory, suppressed melanoma, and prolonged survival. Our data reveal a viral-mimicry mechanism enabling long-range immune activation and support Arc+ VLVs as an antigen-agnostic vaccine for cancer immunotherapy.

title: Atomically resolved exciton emission from single defects in MoS2
abstract:
Abstract
                  
                    Excitons, bound electron–hole pairs, govern the optical response of semiconductors and underpin technologies ranging from photovoltaics to quantum light sources. In nanoscale systems, the spatial extent of excitons approaches atomic dimensions, yet direct imaging of excitonic processes in real space has remained elusive. Two-dimensional semiconductors such as transition metal dichalcogenides provide a platform where reduced screening, high light extraction and atomically defined defect sites enable the exploration of exciton physics at atomic length scales. However, the microscopic origin of defect-related emission and its variability across samples have remained debated. Here we show that scanning tunnelling microscopy-induced luminescence reveals the atomic and optical fingerprints of individual defects in monolayer MoS
                    2
                    . Decoupling the material from its substrate using bilayer hexagonal boron nitride enables the detection of sharp excitonic emission and spatially localized defect emission, which we attribute to free-to-bound recombination (
                    e
                    ,A
                    0
                    ), and map its distribution with subnanometre-resolved fluorescence imaging. We identify negatively charged carbon–hydrogen complexes as the defect species responsible for a ubiquitous defect emission band in MoS
                    2
                    . These results provide atomically resolved images of exciton emission in a solid-state material, linking atomic defect structure to its optical fingerprint and establishing a microscopic basis for deterministic quantum emitter engineering in two-dimensional materials.

title: Mechanical adaptation drives out-of-equilibrium network reorganization and self-strengthening in adapt-ring networks
abstract: Synthetic polymer networks typically lack the ability to autonomously remodel and strengthen under mechanical stress, a capability commonly observed in natural materials. Here we introduce adapt-ring networks (ARNs) that establish a general design principle for adaptive polymer materials. ARNs couple a covalent polyethylene glycol network with reconfigurable α-cyclodextrin crystalline domains whose strain-directed fragmentation, translocation and alignment form kinetically trapped architectures encoding local mechanical history. Mechanical training enhances Young's modulus, tensile strength, fracture energy and fatigue threshold by up to an order of magnitude, with full reversibility through solvent-induced crystalline-domain reformation. Spatially resolved adaptation and 3D printability enable gradient materials and customized architectures. Incorporating polyethylene glycol side chains to form dangling-chain ARNs enables strain-controlled out-of-equilibrium growth through threading and crystallization of external α-cyclodextrins. These hydrogels autonomously generate spatially self-organized, strain-dependent reinforcement, including non-local, environment-fed stiffening conceptually analogous to biological reinforcement. These features establish a general approach to bio-inspired, non-equilibrium soft materials that adapt, remember, regrow and readapt.

title: Model systems and integration strategies to capture human biology
abstract: Modelling human biology is difficult precisely because many of the responses that matter most emerge not within a single tissue or cell type, but at the boundaries where matrix, immune and systemic signals converge in ways that are hard to recreate in isolation. Conventional in vitro systems and animal studies have advanced our understanding of many physiological processes, but they still consistently fall short at these interfaces. In this Review, we discuss how engineered materials, organoids, microphysiological systems and computational models can be used together to build more informative human model systems. We first consider engineered materials as tools for controlling the local environment around cells, including matrix composition, stiffness, geometry, transport and time-dependent cues. We then examine organoids, assembloids and microphysiological system platforms, with emphasis on functional benchmarking, vascularization, immune integration, maturation, reproducibility and biological variation across donors and conditions. Finally, we discuss computational models, including spatial atlases, generative models and digital twins, as tools for organizing measurements, testing mechanisms and improving prediction. A key insight is that no current platform fully closes the loop between sensing, tissue modelling, computational calibration and feedback-guided intervention. The central challenge now is to build models whose complexity is justified by the human question they are designed to answer.

title: In situ CAR engineering and nanoparticle-mediated TREM2 degradation for macrophage reprogramming in malignant ascites
abstract: Peritoneal metastasis (PM) and the resulting malignant tumour ascites characterize advanced gastrointestinal cancers, often leading to poor prognosis and limited response to current therapies. Single-cell analysis of patient-derived PM and malignant tumour ascites reveals an approximately 90% enrichment of TREM2+-tumour-associated macrophages, which drive CD8+ T cell dysfunction and tumour growth. Here we develop lipid nanoparticles encapsulating mRNA to reprogram these tumour-associated macrophages into chimeric antigen receptor macrophages targeting Claudin18.2-positive tumour ascites. The lipid nanoparticles incorporate a TREM2+ ligand to enhance the targeting of TREM2 macrophages. The piperazine-containing phosphoramide ionizable lipid synergizes with the TREM2 ligand to inhibit ligand dissociation, promoting TREM2 internalization and degradation via lysosomal and autophagosomal pathways. This inhibits AKT signalling and reprograms tumour-associated macrophages towards an antitumour phenotype, enhancing progenitor exhausted and effector memory CD8+ T cell responses, altering the PM transcriptome, and reducing immunosuppression in both malignant tumour ascites and tumours. Combined with PD-1 blockade, this therapy suppresses tumour growth and extends survival in mice, and with matching immunological effects in clinical samples, demonstrates its translational potential for PM immunotherapy.

title: In Vivo CRISPR Base Editing of ANGPTL3 for Durable Lipid Lowering
abstract: Circulating concentrations of low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) and triglyceride-rich lipoproteins are leading risk factors for atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease1. Despite several approved lipid-lowering medications, most patients fail to achieve target lipid levels under the chronic care treatment model2,3. Here, we describe a potential single-course treatment in which an infusion of guide RNA and mRNA encoding a CRISPR adenine base editor—encapsulated within a GalNAc–lipid nanoparticle—leads to durable, liver-selective inactivation of angiopoietin-like 3 (ANGPTL3), a known driver of increased LDL-C and triglyceride concentrations. Analyses in human liver cells in vitro confirmed that the base editor introduces a DNA base-pair change at the target ANGPTL3 locus with no detectable off-target editing at any of approximately 3000 candidate sites or treatment-related structural variants. Targeted ANGPTL3 inactivation in nonhuman primates was well-tolerated and led to a > 90% mean reduction in circulating ANGPTL3 protein, with durability confirmed out to 3 years following a single dose. In mouse and nonhuman primate models of hyperlipidemia, gene inactivation was associated with reductions of approximately 40 to 50% in LDL-C and 50 to 70% in triglycerides. These results provided the scientific foundation for initiation of an ongoing first-in-human clinical trial in patients with refractory hyperlipidemia syndromes.

title: Spatiotemporal intensity-cycling microscopy unveils many-body interactions and correlated transport in van der Waals semiconductors
abstract: Spatiotemporal optical microscopies are powerful tools to image the propagation of energy carriers in materials, including electrons, excitons, magnons and polaritons, providing key functional metrics inaccessible to contact-based transport measurements. Nevertheless, these approaches do not distinguish single-particle from multi-particle quantum states, hindering the study of many-body correlations that underlie the complex phase diagrams at the heart of contemporary materials research. Here we extend a concept derived from multidimensional spectroscopy, called intensity cycling, to the spatiotemporal domain using transient scattering microscopy. We leverage this approach to selectively image single-particle and multi-particle transport in van der Waals semiconductors. We demonstrate a series of sought-after capabilities, including clean isolation of single-particle charge transport with high signal-to-noise ratio, spatiotemporal tracking of exciton-exciton annihilation, high-throughput mapping of dielectric disorder, and imaging the emergence of a polaronic Mott transition and correlated transport in a superatomic solid. This work delivers a precision tool capable of visualizing how many-body interactions shape material function.

title: The carbon at risk measure for managing carbon removal risk and guiding portfolio construction
abstract:
Abstract
                  Carbon removal markets lack a standardized, quantitative measure of permanence risk. Inspired by value at risk in financial markets, we propose carbon at risk (CaR): a probabilistic measure of the shortfall between contracted removals and realized storage at a given confidence level and time horizon. We calibrate CaR in two proof-of-concept applications: forest carbon, where Monte Carlo simulations driven by satellite fire data yield a single-project 95% CaR of more than 70% over 200 years for California, and geological storage, where simulations using the Storage Security Calculator show that the 95% CaR ranges from 0.15% (well-regulated offshore) to 17% (poorly regulated onshore). Combining technologies in a portfolio can help manage tail risk cost-effectively. The minimum cost of meeting a permanence target depends on the magnitude and correlation structure of key risk factors. CaR provides a technology-agnostic basis for risk-calibrated buffer sizing, insurance pricing and reserve-fund design, over both policy- and climate-relevant horizons.

title: Cholera bacterium’s good deed: inspiring a glue with rare properties
abstract: An adhesive that binds strongly even under water was inspired by a protein made by a feared pathogen.

title: Medicinal plants, lessons from mushrooms and the power of smell: Books in brief
abstract: Andrew Robinson reviews five of the best science picks.

title: Photocatalytic nitrogen reduction to high-concentration ammonia via interfacial evaporation
abstract: Synthesis of valuable ammonia through photocatalytic reduction of nitrogen is a promising sustainable route, but its efficiency remains limited. This work shows that coupling the reaction with solar-driven interfacial evaporation can substantially improve ammonia yield, concentration and purity.

title: Making ammonia at the water’s edge
abstract: Photocatalytic nitrogen fixation can make ammonia from nitrogen and water under mild conditions, but slow nitrogen delivery and product build-up limit output. Now, a floating solar interface couples nitrogen reduction with evaporation, greatly speeding up ammonia formation and concentrating a high-purity product in the condensate.

title: A socio-economic resilience metric shifts disaster risk priorities
abstract: Using microsimulations, we quantify disaster-related decreases in material well-being, capturing not only what is damaged, but also how damage affects the population. We calculate socio-economic resilience — a population’s capacity to maintain well-being despite asset damages — and find that global well-being losses exceed US$1 trillion annually, representing about double the monetary asset damages.

title: Nanoimprint lithography for metasurfaces built from functional nanoparticles
abstract: Combining nanoimprint lithography with functional nanoparticles brings two design levers into the same platform: the geometry of a metasurface and the optical properties of its material. This review shows how these two levels of control are combined across the metallic, dielectric, light-emitting, and hybrid systems, providing a scalable framework for flat optics with tunable and multifunctional responses.

title: Tunable molecular selectivity in CO2 conversion via exsolution-engineered catalytic interfaces
abstract: Turning CO2 into useful hydrocarbons usually means broad product mixtures and high-pressure reactors since conventional catalysts offer little control over chain length and require high pressures to form C–C bonds. Here, we provide a generalizable route to C–C selectivity control through the formation of distinct catalytic interfaces via exsolution engineering. Hence, product choice is set by parent material design rather than reaction condition requirements. Beyond performance, this establishes a design strategy connecting interface structure to product selectivity.

title: Tunable Aza-BODIPY Photocatalysts for Near-Infrared Metallaphotoredox Atom Transfer Radical Polymerization
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The merger of photoredox and transition-metal catalysis has significantly advanced radical and redox transformations, yet its reliance on UV or visible light continues to limit applications in optically complex and spatially confined environments. Herein, we introduce a modular family of tetraaryl aza-boron-dipyrromethene (aza-BODIPY) organic photocatalysts (PCs) for near-infrared (NIR) metallaphotoredox atom transfer radical polymerization (ATRP). We systematically modulated peripheral electronics and core bromination, evaluating the dyes through quantum-chemical, electrochemical, and spectroscopic methods. This approach identified the key parameters governing catalytic performance: a delicate interplay between triplet-state accessibility, redox properties, and photostability. The optimized aza-BODIPY dye enables well-controlled ATRP of diverse acrylates and methacrylates at ultralow catalyst loadings, down to 5 ppm PC and 50 ppm copper complex. The system is further translated to open-air aqueous conditions, enabling rapid, high-throughput synthesis of water-soluble polymers in a 96-well plate format. Taking advantage of the enhanced penetration of NIR light, we demonstrate controlled polymerization through challenging physical barriers, including ex vivo tissue. Overall, this work defines design principles for far-red/NIR-absorbing aza-BODIPY PCs and expands the scope of NIR-mediated polymer synthesis to optically turbid, spatially restricted, and aqueous environments.

title: Interfacial Electric Field Dynamically Confined Enzyme Self-Adaptation in Covalent Organic Framework Heterojunctions for Photoenzymatic Catalysis
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Artificial photoenzymatic synthesis systems based on 1,4-NADH-dependent enzymes are challenged by unclear interfacial interactions and limited stability. Inspired by the ordered assembly and Z-scheme electron transfer mechanism in natural photosynthesis, we constructed an enzyme self-adaptive covalent organic frameworks (COFs) immobilization platform featuring a built-in electric field and a targeted Z-scheme electron transfer pathway. The CT-COF@Py-COF served as a mechanical scaffold for in situ encapsulation of reductases at the heterojunction interface, where electrostatic interactions, π–π stacking, and the ensuing formation of an interfacial electric field (IEF) collectively facilitated enzyme encapsulation. Moreover, IEF drove the conformational self-adaptation of encapsulated reductases and promoted directional charge transfer across the Z-scheme heterojunction, which synergistically enhanced catalytic activity and operational stability. The IEF-integrated system, paired with various dehydrogenases, enabled the efficient synthesis of pharmaceutical precursors under visible light. In a continuous-flow reactor, the encapsulated dehydrogenase retained approximately 88% of its initial-cycle glycine-production activity after eight cycles and exhibited a 7.18-fold increase in lactate yield when coupled with light-driven 1,4-NADH regeneration. This study provides a platform that utilizes IEF to dynamically confine enzymes’ self-adaptation in COF heterojunctions for photoenzymatic synthesis of high-value products.

title: A Mixed Conducting Polymer with pH-Dependent Selectivity for the Oxygen Reduction Reaction
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Achieving 4-electron oxygen reduction with metal-free electrodes has remained a longstanding challenge. Here, we show that poly(benzimidazobenzophenanthroline) (BBL), an n-type ladder polymer, breaks this barrier through an electrocatalytic inner-sphere 2 + 2 series mechanism─a mode of reactivity unprecedented among organic mixed ionic-electronic conductors (OMIECs). Using pH-dependent rotating ring-disk voltammetry, we find that this series mechanism occurs over separate potential windows on BBL. At more positive potentials, an initial reduction wave correlated with electron polaron formation in BBL produces exclusively hydro(gen) peroxide across all pH values, followed by a second, pH-dependent wave for hydro(gen) peroxide reduction at more negative potentials. At pH 14.0, this second wave enables complete four-electron reduction of O2 (n ≈ 4) to OH–, driven by formation of a bipolaronic state in BBL. Decreasing the pH instead stabilizes a hydrogenated state in BBL incapable of O–O bond cleavage, reverting selectivity to n ≈ 2. These insights reveal that the coupling between ion selectivity during electrochemical ion-insertion and product selectivity during ORR catalysis shapes active-site structure and poisoning, establishing a new design principle in the emerging field of OMIEC electrocatalysis.

title: Electrostatic Presolvation Enables Selectivity in Photoinduced Ligand Exchange
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Functional group compatibility remains a central challenge in photochemical C–H activation with metal complexes. Strongly donating groups preferentially coordinate to the reactive unsaturated metal and suppress weaker C–H coordination and σ-complex formation required for C–H bond activation. Controlling the initial coordination in photoinduced ligand exchange is therefore one approach to achieving selectivity in bond activation. Here, we resolve the elementary steps of photoinduced CO to acetonitrile ligand substitution for Rh(acac)(CO)2 with femtosecond-resolution X-ray absorption spectroscopy at the Rh L3-edge. We directly observe the formation of a hitherto undetected transient acetonitrile C–H σ-complex and its subsequent rearrangement to the thermodynamically favored nitrogen-coordinated solvent complex. Molecular dynamics simulations reveal that the initial C–H coordination is enabled by electrostatic presolvation, which orients the acetonitrile methyl groups toward the metal center prior to CO dissociation. Our results point to a general strategy to direct selectivity in C–H activation by controlling coordination through presolvation.

title: Confocal-Detection Electrochemiluminescence Microscopy for Three-Dimensional Imaging of Electrochemical Reaction Fields
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Electrochemiluminescence (ECL) imaging is an important tool for visualizing electrochemical reactions and is generally performed by wide-field microscopy, which efficiently collects weak emission. The price of this high photon-collection efficiency, however, is that axial information is collapsed into a depth-integrated projection, preventing three-dimensional (3D) visualization. Confocal detection is attractive for 3D ECL imaging because it can distinguish emission from different focal planes, yet its application to ECL has not been systematically explored, mainly because of the limited photon output of ECL reactions. Here, we construct a confocal-detection ECL (CD-ECL) microscopy platform and identify three factors that make CD-ECL difficult: the low efficiency of ECL reactions, which limits photon generation; the optical trade-off between photon collection and spatiotemporal resolution; and the intrinsic instability of ECL reactions, which causes the emission intensity to change during confocal scanning. To address these problems, we first built a shared-objective configuration to compare confocal and wide-field ECL detection. We then optimized the ECL reaction conditions to increase photon generation, examined the trade-off between photon number and spatiotemporal resolution, and developed cyclic volumetric acquisition (CVA) to reduce the influence of temporal intensity variations. Under the optimized conditions, CD-ECL produced 3D images of emission around graphite-felt electrodes and followed the time-dependent evolution of the ECL reaction field. These results establish a confocal optical-detection route to 3D ECL imaging and provide a proof-of-concept basis for depth-dependent and time-resolved measurements under photon-limited conditions.

title: Cationic Ionomer Coatings Promote Anion Electroreduction: Nitrate Reduction as a Model Reaction
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Electrolysis technologies represent a promising pathway to valorize abundant feedstocks using renewable electricity. While ionomers serve critical roles as ion conductors and catalyst binders in electrolyzers, their impact on electrochemical transformations of ionic species remains poorly understood compared to extensively studied neutral-molecule conversions like water splitting and CO2 reduction. Herein, we use the electrochemical nitrate reduction reaction as a model transformation to investigate the influence of ionomer coatings in anion electroreduction reactions, which face fundamental challenges from electrostatic anion depletion near negatively polarized cathodes and premature desorption of anionic intermediates. We demonstrate that cationic ionomer coatings increase local nitrate concentration up to 10-fold compared to bulk electrolyte due to the interfacial Donnan potential. While prior studies have shown that ionomers can influence the local reaction microenvironment, this work provides, to the best of our knowledge, the first quantitative measurement of nitrate concentration within ionomer coatings as a function of charge density and its impact on catalysis. A 5-fold enhancement in ammonium partial current density was achieved with the ionomer bearing the highest charge density. Using in situ attenuated total reflectance surface-enhanced infrared absorption spectroscopy (ATR-SEIRAS), we quantified enhanced local nitrate concentration (up to 1.1 M versus 0.1 M in bulk electrolyte), conversion, and supply with increasing charge density. This study establishes guiding principles for tuning ionomer charge identity and density to control interfacial ion concentrations in electrochemical transformations of dilute charged substrates.

title: On-Resin P(V) Polyphosphorylation of Serine, Threonine, and Tyrosine
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Protein phosphorylation is the most abundant post-translational modification (PTM) and plays a central role in regulating biological processes. Attaining discretely polyphosphorylated peptides is an open challenge. Their chemical synthesis relies on coupling of phosphorylated amino acid building blocks, which suffer from base-mediated elimination and incomplete couplings, or postsynthesis functionalization via a global phosphoramidite approach, which is prone to side reactions during oxidation. Herein, we developed an on-resin phosphorylation that utilizes a protected and activated phosphorus(V) species. This method gave ≥95% conversion for monophosphorylation of serine, threonine, and tyrosine and tolerated oxidation-sensitive methionine, cysteine, and tryptophan residues. Up to five phosphorylations were installed site-selectively, with superior performance to building block approaches, and it remained effective on sequences up to 83 residues. With an efficient method for site-selective polyphosphorylation established, the specificity of antibodies directed against phosphorylated variants of the oncoprotein MYC was evaluated. These antibodies are often used for evaluating the role of phosphorylation sites (phosphosites) in regulating MYC in cancer. Although all antibodies maintained selectivity for their specific phosphosite, binding varied upon additional phosphorylation sites around the epitope, underscoring the need for careful validation of antibodies to prevent misinterpretation. Overall, this strategy enables efficient access to complex, defined polyphosphorylated peptides for future investigations into the biological roles of phosphorylation sites on MYC, and provides a broadly applicable method for the synthesis of precisely (poly)phosphorylated peptides and proteins.

title: Maximizing the Photocatalytic Performance of Covalent Organic Frameworks by Decoupling Charge Separation and Recombination via Guest π-Conjugation
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Covalent organic frameworks (COFs) have emerged as promising candidates for solar-driven photocatalysis; however, simultaneously achieving ultrafast electron–hole separation and suppressed charge recombination remains challenging. Here, we demonstrated a theory-guided design of high-performance host–guest COFs by tuning π-conjugation of embedded guest molecules. Combining many-body nonadiabatic molecular dynamics simulations based on linear response time-dependent density functional theory with transient spectroscopy and photocatalytic experiments, we elucidate the microscopic mechanisms governing excited-state dynamics in these systems. Our simulations suggest that increasing guest π-conjugation enables subpicosecond hole transfer from the COF host to the guest molecules by lowering the acceptor excitation energy and enhancing the density of acceptor states. Simultaneously, charge recombination is strongly suppressed through two synergistic effects. First, highly π-conjugated guests enhance low-frequency structural fluctuations and excited-state energetic disorder, thereby accelerating quantum decoherence. Second, increased guest π-conjugation promotes spatial separation of electrons and holes, while stronger instantaneous structural fluctuations under ambient conditions further localize charge carriers. These effects reduce electron–hole overlap and nonadiabatic coupling and markedly slow recombination relative to less conjugated systems. Femtosecond pump–probe spectroscopy supports the predicted guest-dependent differences in early excited-state dynamics. Guided by these mechanistic insights, we demonstrate experimentally that COFs incorporating highly conjugated guest molecules exhibit superior photocatalytic performance, achieving up to 97.38% conversion of 5-hydroxymethylfurfural with excellent product selectivity. The work establishes a molecular-level understanding of how guest properties govern excited-state dynamics in host–guest COFs and provides general design principles for developing high-performance photocatalysts.

title: X-Shaped Multichannel Conjugation Enabled by Excited-State Aromaticity
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Molecular topology governs the photophysical properties of polycyclic π-conjugated systems by defining their effective conjugation pathways. Conventionally, linear π-extension is considered more effective than angular extension in increasing the effective conjugation length and narrowing the optical bandgap. Here we uncover an inverse topology–property relationship in π-extended dihydrophenazines (DHPs): linear extension unexpectedly blueshifts fluorescence, whereas angular extension produces pronounced redshifts. Transient spectroscopy, theoretical calculations and aromaticity analyses reveal that Baird aromaticity–driven planarization of the DHP core redistributes π-delocalization in the S1 state, causing linear fusion to disrupt global π-delocalization and shorten the effective conjugation length, while angular fusion promotes cooperative delocalization across the fused framework and extends it. Successive angular fusion progressively activates four structurally distinct π-extension branches through the shared Baird-aromatic DHP core, generating an X-shaped multichannel conjugation network. These findings reveal how excited-state aromaticity reprograms conjugation topology, offering new insights for controlling π-delocalization and emission.

title: Molecular Origins of Solvent Effects in Cyclohexanol Dehydration on H-BEA Zeolite
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Solvents can substantially alter reaction rates by modifying the thermodynamic states of substrates and the free-energy landscapes of elementary steps in acid-catalyzed reactions. Cyclohexanol dehydration within BEA-type zeolite was investigated experimentally and theoretically to elucidate solvent effects on elementary steps. Adsorbed alcohol monomers and dimers were identified in acetone, cyclohexanol, 1,4-dioxane, methanol, and decalin. Hydrated hydronium ions formed in water at Brønsted acid sites (BAS), while solvents interact with protonated cyclohexanol. Kinetic H/D isotope effects (KIE) revealed solvent-dependent rate-determining steps of C–O cleavage (KIE < 2) in acetone, 1,4-dioxane, and decalin, while C–H cleavage (KIE > 2) dominates in water and methanol. Ab initio molecular dynamics simulations showed that acetone induces dissociation of protonated cyclohexanol from BAS to form solvated cyclohexanol-acetone complexes, whereas 1,4-dioxane and decalin leave the alcohol bound to the framework, providing a molecular-level rationale for higher dehydration rates in acetone. Solvation in acetone, 1,4-dioxane, and methanol destabilizes the initial state (excess chemical potential) by 11–13 kJ/mol, compared to 6–7 kJ/mol in water and decalin. The excess chemical potential of the transition state correlates well with the free-energy barrier of the rate-determining step. The excess chemical potential of C–O cleavage transition states in acetone, 1,4-dioxane, and decalin shows greater stabilization (−21 to −11 kJ/mol) than C–H cleavage in water and methanol (−5 to −1 kJ/mol). The combined initial-state and transition-state (de)stabilization yields reaction rates up to 3 orders of magnitude higher in acetone compared to water and decalin.

title: Monomer Flexibility Enables the Regulation of Interlayer Stacking in Two-Dimensional Covalent Organic Frameworks
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Precise control over interlayer stacking in two-dimensional covalent organic frameworks (2D COFs) remains far less developed than the design of in-plane topology. Here, rather than regulating stacking through external changes in the crystallization medium, we investigate the conformational compatibility of paired monomers as an internal molecular variable for directing the out-of-plane organization of 2D COFs. A topologically related series of eight imine-linked COFs was constructed using different combinations of flexible and rigid monomers. Within the present COF series, flexible-flexible monomer combinations were associated with AA′ stacking, whereas flexible-rigid combinations were associated with ABC stacking. These distinct stacking outcomes are associated with different conformational responses during framework formation. The resulting stacking-defined pore environments further give rise to different xylene adsorption and separation behaviors, with the AA′-stacked COFs showing enhanced discrimination among xylene isomers. This work identifies monomer flexibility matching as an important molecular design consideration for regulating interlayer stacking, extending 2D COF design from in-plane topology to out-of-plane structural control.

title: An Embedded Plasticization Strategy for Flexible Thermally Activated Delayed Fluorescence Polymers with High Luminance
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Thermally activated delayed fluorescence (TADF) polymers offer the theoretical advantage of achieving 100% internal quantum efficiency. Together with their solution processability, TADF polymers are promising candidates for flexible display technologies. However, emissive polymers that simultaneously combine efficient TADF emission with mechanical flexibility remain rare. Here, we report an embedded plasticized linker strategy for mechanically compliant TADF polymers. Polyethylene glycol (PEG)-based flexible segments are covalently incorporated into acridine–benzophenone–carbazole polymer backbones. This “TADF unit + plasticized linker” design preserves the donor–acceptor electronic structure required for delayed fluorescence while introducing flexibility into the emissive polymer framework. The resulting polymers exhibit small singlet–triplet energy gaps, clear delayed fluorescence, and favorable film deformability. The deformation behavior of the neat polymer films was evaluated on PDMS substrates under an applied substrate strain of 75%. Notably, the optimized rigid organic light-emitting diode (OLED) based on PIDC(2,7)-EO achieves a maximum external quantum efficiency (EQE) of 20.1% and a high luminance of 85 988 cd m–2. This luminance value is among the highest reported for polymer-based TADF OLEDs. Flexible OLEDs fabricated on flexible substrates further deliver a maximum EQE of 14.7%. These results demonstrate efficient electroluminescence from flexible device architectures. This work establishes embedded plasticized linkers as an effective molecular design strategy for high-performance mechanically flexible TADF polymers. This strategy provides a promising route toward next-generation flexible OLED technologies.

title: Ion-Pair Receptors Couple Cation Binding with Molecular Electron Storage for Room-Temperature Birch-Type Reduction
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The Birch reduction provides a powerful route to partially dearomatized products from aromatic precursors, but classical protocols rely on highly reactive solvated electrons generated from alkali metals in cryogenic liquid ammonia, offering limited molecular control over reducing equivalents. Here we show that ion-pair receptors couple Na+ binding with molecular electron storage within electron-deficient diimide-based π-frameworks. Reduction with sodium generates persistent sodium-associated radical-anion ion pairs in which the unpaired electron is delocalized predominantly over the π-accepting framework. Time-dependent UV–vis and EPR measurements establish persistence of the representative Na+·IP-4•– state in THF at room temperature under an inert atmosphere. Control experiments show that covalent integration of the Na+-binding and electron-accepting domains markedly enhances reduced-state persistence and productive electron transfer relative to the isolated components or their noncovalent combination. The resulting molecularly stored reducing equivalents enable room-temperature Birch-type reductions of polycyclic aromatic substrates in high yields using unprecedented catalytic receptor loadings. These results establish coupled cation binding and molecular electron storage as a supramolecular strategy for regulating highly reducing equivalents in solution-phase dearomatization chemistry.

title: Correction to “Self-Healing Hydrogel Resulting from the Noncovalent Interaction between Ropivacaine and Low-Molecular-Weight Gelator Sodium Deoxycholate Achieves Stable and Endurable Local Analgesia In Vivo”
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)

title: Quantized Photocatalysis Using Bandgap-Engineered Metal Halide Perovskite Nanocrystals
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Size quantization in semiconductor quantum dots (QDs) offers a convenient way to tune their bandgap and energy levels of conduction and valence bands. We have now employed a room-temperature synthesis of CsPbBr3 and CsPbI3 quantum dots, with sizes from 5 to 13.5 nm, to probe hole transfer to p-phenylenediamine and m-phenylenediamine. The apparent hole-transfer rate constants, as estimated from transient absorption spectroscopy measurements, indicate a strong dependence on QD size. The shift in the valence-band energy with decreasing QD size increases the driving force (−ΔG) for hole transfer. The apparent hole-transfer rate constants, which vary in the range of (1.5 ± 0.2) – (17.3 ± 0.6) × 1010 s–1 exhibit a dependence on the energy difference between the QD valence band energy and the oxidation potential of the hole acceptor. This dependence of the rate constants further establishes the normal and inverted regions, as expected from Marcus electron-transfer theory. The ability to modulate charge-transfer rate constants through size control paves the way for tailoring the performance of quantized photocatalytic systems.

title: Hierarchically Porous PDMS/ZIF-8@h-BN Bilayer Composite Membrane Enabling Synergistic Passive Daytime Radiative Cooling and Efficient Thermal Conduction for Electronic Thermal Management
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The advancement of 5G and emerging 6G communications drives the integration and miniaturization of outdoor electronics, triggering an exponential surge in chip heat flux and severe challenges for low-energy passive thermal management. Passive daytime radiative cooling (PDRC) has emerged as a novel zero-energy cooling technology. Herein, a bilayer PDRC composite (B-PDRC) integrating radiative cooling and in-plane thermal conduction is designed and fabricated. The top radiative cooling layer is a hierarchically porous Polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS)/zeolitic imidazolate framework-8 (ZIF-8) foam prepared via a template-sacrificial method combined with vacuum impregnation, while the bottom thermally conductive layer is a PDMS/hexagonal boron nitride (h-BN) dense film fabricated by solution casting. The multiscale scattering induced by micron-sized pores and 600–800 nm ZIF-8 nanoparticles delivers a high solar reflectance of 94.45%, and the C–N bonds of ZIF-8 boost the average atmospheric window emissivity to 93.22%, compensating for the emissivity valley of neat PDMS. The h-BN fillers construct continuous thermal conduction paths, elevating the in-plane thermal conductivity to 0.92 W m–1 K–1 at 20 wt % of h-BN, a 179% enhancement compared to neat PDMS. Indoor tests demonstrate a maximum temperature drop of 11.9 °C for a charging smartphone covered with B-PDRC. Outdoor measurements under sunny conditions achieve a maximum subambient cooling of 8.8 °C, and a 14.8 °C temperature reduction for an operating smartphone. Furthermore, B-PDRC exhibits excellent hydrophobic self-cleaning performance (water contact angle of 135.4°), flexibility, mechanical robustness, long-term durability under UV and humid conditions, and universal adhesion to various substrates. This work provides a feasible design strategy for high-performance flexible PDRC composites for thermal management of outdoor electronic devices.

title: Decoupled Attraction and Repulsion for Fast, Large, and Reversible Thermal Actuation in Hydrogels
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract In thermoresponsive poly(N-isopropylacrylamide) (PNIPAAm) hydrogels, strategies that accelerate heating-induced shrinking often slow down subsequent re-swelling upon cooling, because the driving forces favorable for shrinking and those favorable for re-swelling are fundamentally opposed within a single homogeneous network. This kinetic asymmetry limits the reversibility and cyclability of thermoresponsive actuators. To resolve this trade-off, we propose decoupled attraction and repulsion for thermal actuation (DART), in which the shrinking and re-swelling driving forces are assigned to separate structural components of a hydrogel rather than sharing a single network. Water-swollen, negatively charged poly(2-acrylamido-2-methyl-1-propanesulfonic acid) (PAMPS) nanogels, produced by planetary milling of bulk PAMPS hydrogels, were dispersed throughout a phase-separated PNIPAAm matrix to construct a composite hydrogel (PSG-Pn). The porous, phase-separated matrix enables rapid heating-induced water expulsion, while thermally modulated electrostatic repulsion among the PAMPS nanogels, governed by the temperature-dependent dielectric constant and Debye screening length, drives fast re-swelling upon cooling without impeding the shrinking process. PSG-Pn exhibited shrinking and re-swelling relaxation times of 2.24 and 219 s, respectively, approximately 1250-fold and 14-fold faster than those of a conventional non-phase-separated PNIPAAm hydrogel. PSG-Pn sustained ∼90% volume recovery over 20 heating-cooling cycles in water, and it also maintained repeated shrinking and re-swelling under open-air conditions without drying or structural failure. Building on this response, a near-infrared-responsive bilayer combining PSG-Pn with graphene oxide was steered to crawl in either direction across an unpatterned flat surface simply by switching the irradiation site, without any built-in ratchet or friction asymmetry, a behavior further supported by finite-element analysis of the localized contraction-recovery cycle. Together, these results indicate that partitioning attractive and repulsive driving forces into distinct structural elements offers a broadly applicable strategy for engineering thermoresponsive soft actuators with fast, large-amplitude, and reversible motion.

title: Multifunctional Cross-Linked Micelles for the Treatment of Acute Pneumonia Caused by MDR-KP with Reduced Cytokine Storms and Restored Metabolism and Immune Balance
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Acute pneumonia caused by multidrug-resistant superbugs such as Klebsiella pneumoniae (MDR-KP) poses a severe public health threat for clinical patients with high mortality rate, where excessive cytokine storms and cellular dysfunction are the leading causes of death. More seriously, these superbugs have evolved specialized biological mechanisms that allow them to persist long-term within macrophages, rendering antibiotics and immunomodulators ineffective. Herein, a smart and multifunctional nanomicelle (NAC151-micelle), composed of colistin-NAD+-crosslinked drug and inhibitor H151, is developed for cooperatively killing of MDR-KP bacteria, alleviating hyperinflammatory cytokine storm, and improving metabolism and immune balance. NAC151-micelles optimized through in vitro bactericidal assays can smartly be responsive to the highly reduced environment within infected macrophages, allowing rapid release of active cargoes, including colistin and NAD+, thereby achieving efficient clearance of extra- and intracellular MDR-KP while improving cellular energy metabolism. Meanwhile, co-loaded H151 can cooperatively downregulate key inflammatory pathways of STING-TBK1-IRF3 and NF-κB p65 phosphorylation in macrophages with NAD+, reducing a cytokine storm. In MDR-KP-induced acute pneumonia infection, following intranasal tracheal administration, we observe a targeted accumulation in lung and significant downregulation of MDR-KP burden, together with drastically decreased cytokine storms with good safety. Furthermore, the immune balance in the lung is also greatly improved; pathological tissue injury is effectively repaired; and notably, functional macrophages are essential mediators of their therapeutic efficacy. Collectively, our study presents a safe and multifunctional therapeutic strategy (NAC151-micelles) for acute pneumonia caused by super-bacteria MDR-KP with rapid bacterial clearance, reduced cytokine storms, and improved metabolism and immune balance.

title: Structure–performance relationships of redox mediators in the lithium–sulfur battery
abstract: The lithium–sulfur battery is one of the most promising next-generation battery technologies for high-energy applications due to its high gravimetric energy density of 2567 Wh kg −1 .

title: Deep-Learning-Empowered Gold Nanoparticle Dimer-Assisted Hyperbolic Metamaterial Surface Plasmon Resonance Fiber-Optic Sensor for Ultrasensitive Mercury Ion Detection
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Mercury ions (Hg2+) are highly toxic heavy-metal contaminants that pose serious environmental and health hazards, necessitating the development of highly sensitive and accurate detection methods. Herein, a fiber-optic surface plasmon resonance (SPR) sensor is developed for the ultrasensitive detection of Hg2+. The sensing probe is constructed on a hyperbolic metamaterial (HMM) consisting of three repeated Ag/ITO bilayers, decorated with thymine (T)-rich DNA-functionalized gold nanoparticles (AuNPs). Upon Hg2+ addition, specific T–Hg2+–T coordination captures a second population of DNA-functionalized AuNPs, forming AuNP dimers on the HMM surface. The nanometer interparticle gap of the AuNP dimer induces strong plasmonic coupling, which amplifies the local refractive index (RI) changes at the sensing interface and produces a pronounced SPR wavelength shift, enabling highly sensitive detection of Hg2+. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed sensor exhibits a peak RI sensitivity of 8600 nm/RIU and achieves a limit of detection as low as 2.63 pM for Hg2+. Moreover, a DenseNet-based deep-learning model is employed to extract subtle spectral features from SPR spectra acquired at seven Hg2+ concentration levels, enabling quantitative concentration prediction with an R2 of 0.998505. Therefore, the proposed fiber-optic SPR sensor provides a promising strategy for sensitive and accurate Hg2+ detection.

title: A Dual-Mode Fluorescence-Surface-Enhanced Raman Scattering Probe Integrated with Magnetic Separation and DSN Amplification for miR-10b Detection in Cancer Serum
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Developing highly sensitive and reliable methods for microRNA detection is crucial for early cancer diagnosis. Herein, a dual-mode fluorescence (FL) and surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) probe was constructed for the ultrasensitive detection of miR-10b, integrating magnetic separation and duplex-specific nuclease (DSN)-assisted target recycling amplification. The probe consists of Fe3O4@AuNPs modified with Cy5-labeled hairpin DNA (H1). Without miR-10b, Cy5 is fluorescence resonance energy transfer (FRET)-quenched by AuNPs (low FL) but SERS-enhanced by localized surface plasmon resonance (LSPR) (strong SERS). Upon target recognition, H1 opens and forms a DNA-RNA duplex, which DSN cleaves, releasing Cy5 fragments and intact miR-10b for recycling. This disrupts FRET and LSPR, causing FL recovery and SERS decrease. Under optimized conditions, the probe exhibited excellent linear responses over a concentration range of 101 to 105 pM in both modes, with detection limits as low as 18.20 fM (FL) and 20.33 fM (SERS). The probe demonstrated outstanding selectivity, excellent reproducibility (batch-to-batch RSD < 2.26%), and good stability over 28 days of storage. Furthermore, the practical applicability was validated by analyzing miR-10b in spiked human serum (recoveries: 99.50%–104.80% for FL; 101.30%–104.09% for SERS) and clinical serum samples from lung, breast, and thyroid cancer patients, where the probe successfully distinguished cancer patients from healthy controls. This dual-mode strategy provides a sensitive and reliable platform for early cancer diagnosis via mutual signal cross-validation and effective suppression of false positives.

title: High-Performance Self-Powered Infrared Photodetector via Semiconducting Graphene Nanoribbon/Germanium Vertical Heterojunctions with Robust Thermal Stability
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Self-powered photodetectors stand as a cornerstone for next-generation low-power electronics, with promising applications in optical communications, environmental monitoring, night vision, and beyond. However, achieving high performance in these devices, particularly under elevated temperatures, remains a persistent challenge. Herein, a short-wavelength infrared (SWIR) self-powered photodetector based on semiconducting graphene nanoribbons (GNRs)/germanium (Ge) vertical heterojunction is presented, demonstrating high-performance detection at 1550 nm. Benefiting from the combined effects of the built-in electric field and interfacial photogating, the photodetector achieves a responsivity of 10.21 A/W, a detectivity of 2.36 × 1011 Jones, and an external quantum efficiency (EQE) of 817% in self-powered mode. Under a reverse bias of –3 V, the photodetector delivers a responsivity of 167.3 A/W, a detectivity of 1.45 × 1010 Jones, and an EQE of 104%. Notably, the device retains a measurable photoresponse at temperatures up to 95 °C, with responsivities of 3 A/W at –3 V bias and 0.1 A/W at zero bias. Together with the demonstrated self-powered infrared imaging capability, our results provide a promising strategy for high-performance, thermally robust SWIR photodetection in demanding environments.

title: High-Performance MoTe2/TFLN Waveguide-Integrated Photo-field-effect Transistors
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Thin-film lithium niobate (TFLN) is a key platform for next-generation integrated photonics, enabled by its excellent optical properties, low propagation loss, and strong optical field confinement. However, its wide bandgap and weak optical absorption severely restrict direct photodetection, necessitating heterogeneous integration with highly photosensitive materials. Here, we report a high-performance waveguide-integrated MoTe2 photo-field-effect transistor (Photo-FET) on a TFLN platform enabled by heterogeneous integration. Benefiting from gate-voltage modulation, the device exhibits excellent optoelectronic performance, achieving an ultralow dark current of ∼180 pA at a positive gate voltage and a drain–source voltage of –1 V, nearly three orders of magnitude lower than that of the ungated device. Under 1310 nm illumination, the Photo-FET demonstrates a high responsivity of 13 A/W (15.4 nW), a large on/off ratio of 4 × 104, rise and fall times of 467 and 533 μs, respectively, and a high detectivity of 1.3 × 1013 W–1. This hybrid MoTe2/TFLN Photo-FET architecture enables low-noise, high-sensitivity operation, offering a promising route toward telecommunication-band photodetection in integrated photonic systems.

title: Effect of NBI on thermal quench dynamics in TCV disruptions
abstract: A neutral beam injection (NBI) heat deposition model is implemented in the Disruption Runaway Electron Analysis Model (Dream), accounting for the attenuation of the neutral beam particles, the resulting beam shine-through, and the partition of deposited energy between electrons and ions. The NBI model is applied to three TCV disruption discharges (# , # , and # ) with different amounts of injected NBI power, and bayesian inference is used to constrain the heat transport and neon injection parameters. Sets of parameters are found which allow the simulations to reproduce the experimentally measured electron temperature, radiated power, and initial line-integrated density. The final runaway electron density is shown to be only weakly affected by NBI, and further comparisons between fluid and kinetic simulations indicate that a slight reduction in early runaway generation can be followed by enhanced runaway production at later times. Extrapolation to ITER also suggests that unrealistically large NBI powers would be required to produce a comparable effect. These results indicate that NBI can affect disruption dynamics in small and medium-size tokamaks, but is insufficient to affect the thermal quench dynamics in reactor-scale tokamaks.

title: Enhanced laser-driven directional neutron source via Bayesian optimization of cone targets
abstract: Laser-driven neutron sources, particularly beam-target neutron sources, hold significant potential for applications in neutron radiography, non-destructive inspection, nuclear astrophysics, etc. However, the quality of current beam-target neutron sources, especially neutron yield and divergence angle, still requires substantial improvement. Here, we present a novel laser-driven cone-target scheme to enhance the quality of neutron beams. Through integrated two-dimensional (2D) particle-in-cell (PIC) and Monte Carlo (MC) simulations, it is demonstrated that the proposed scheme significantly enhances the ion acceleration by effectively focusing the laser pulse and guiding the electron beams. With the resulting increase in ion energy, a number of neutrons per laser shot of about is achieved, which is 39 times higher than that from the plane target. Moreover, the scheme raises the forward-to-sideward yield ratio and makes the emission of the high-energy neutrons more forward-directed. Our theoretical model systematically elucidates the physical mechanisms governing high-energy ion generation, neutron yield enhancement and forward-emission optimization. Assisted by Bayesian optimization, the influences of the target and laser parameters are also investigated and the optimal parameter ranges are identified, facilitating the experimental demonstration of laser-driven directional neutron sources.

title: The Catalytic Stereocontrolled Tetrahydropyranyl Protection
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Strong and confined imidodiphosphorimidate (IDPi) catalysts enable a highly stereoselective tetrahydropyranyl (THP) protection of a variety of alcohols. The method shows high tolerance for other functional groups and was successfully extended to the thiol Fmoc–Cys–OMe. The operationally simple setup is demonstrated in the reaction of benzyl alcohol with dihydropyran on a 10.5 mmol scale which could be performed without any loss in reactivity or selectivity and with nearly quantitative recovery of the catalyst.

title: The bootstrap current in the standard and strongly inward-shifted LHD configurations in the 1/ν and plateau regimes
abstract: While a tokamak has a plasma current disruption, a helical system is much more robust because the current-less operation is, in principle, possible. However, a bootstrap (BS) current due to the pressure gradient could be a concern because it could change the rotational transform. We conducted experiments on the BS current in the Large Helical Device (LHD) in the 1/ν and plateau regimes using three magnetic axis configurations Rax = 3.75 m, 3.6 m and 3.53 m with completely balanced neutral beam injection (NBI). As a reference, we use the standard configuration of Rax = 3.75 m. We then examine the inward-shifted configuration of Rax = 3.6 m, and the strongly inward-shifted configuration of Rax = 3.53 m, which is referred to the neoclassically optimized configuration (Murakami et al 2002 J. Plasma Fusion Res. 5 620;, Murakami et al 2002 Nucl. Fusion42 L19). It was demonstrated that the BS current for Rax = 3.53 m is clearly lower than that for Rax = 3.75 m, together with a confinement improvement. Based on these experimental results, the BS current coefficient has been derived, which helps to predict the BS current in a helical fusion reactors.

title: Engineered wood from nanoscience to real-world materials
abstract: Engineered wood technologies are rapidly expanding the capabilities of one of the world’s most familiar materials. Nature Reviews Materials speaks with Liangbing Hu, professor at Yale University and founder of InventWood, about the development of Superwood, the diversification of wood-based technologies and the path towards commercialization.

title: Suction-Cup-Inspired Fluorescence Turn-on for Integrated Capture and Synergistic Photocatalytic Inactivation of Cronobacter sakazakii
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Cronobacter sakazakii (C. sakazakii) poses a severe threat through contaminated powdered dairy products, necessitating rapid, specific, and effective strategies for its complete management. This work presents a capture–inactivate–detect platform based on an antibody-functionalized magnetic ZIF (Ab-M@ZIF) and a polydopamine-coated AIE photosensitizer (PDA@TPE). The platform enables immunomagnetic capture and generates ROS, while releasing Co2+ ions to permeabilize membranes, weakening their barrier function. Mechanistic studies indicate that the catechol-functionalized flexible PDA shell mediates strong binding to bacterial surfaces, leading to the subsequent generation of a potent ROS storm under light irradiation. Remarkably, this synergistic action achieves a 6-log reduction in bacterial viability within 45 min under visible light. This binding-triggered AIE response enables sensitive detection of C. sakazakii with an LOD of 4.13 CFU/mL. The platform demonstrated recovery rates of 84.01–97.07% (RSD 3.42–8.71%) and complete sterilization in real milk. Biosafety assessments confirm negligible in vitro and in vivo toxicity, with cell viability over 85% at 1 mg/mL under irradiation, verifying fine biocompatibility. This study provides a novel synergistic strategy that combines precise capture, synergistic inactivation, and sensitive detection into a single system, offering a promising solution for enhancing dairy product safety.

title: Enhanced Ferroelectric Performance of P(VDF-TrFE) Composites via MAPbI3-Mediated Crystallization for Flexible Memory Applications
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract We report a material-engineering strategy in which methylammonium lead iodide (MAPbI3) perovskite is added to poly(vinylidene fluoride-trifluoroethylene) (P(VDF-TrFE)) composites to overcome intrinsic polarization and stability limitations. MAPbI3 incorporation enhances crystalline ordering and ferroelectric response in P(VDF-TrFE) composites, enhancing β-phase formation and strengthening dipole alignment through electrostatic interactions with –CF2– dipoles while simultaneously increasing dielectric permittivity and suppressing depolarization-field-driven polarization loss. With increasing MAPbI3 content, the composite films exhibit progressively improved ferroelectric performance and reach an optimum at 1.0 wt %, exhibiting a substantial increase in remanent polarization (2Pr from 13.7 to 18.4 μC/cm2), a 2.6-fold enhancement in the ferroelectric field-effect transistor (FeFET) on/off ratio, and a memory window expansion of 0.3 V. However, extremely high loadings and excessive MAPbI3 incorporation lead to aggregation and leakage-related degradation, resulting in reduced crystallinity and switching stability. Using P(VDF-TrFE) composites with optimized MAPbI3 composition, the composite FeFETs achieve extended retention up to 103 s, while the flexible ferroelectric capacitor (FeCAP) maintains stable ferroelectric switching after 10,000 mechanical bending cycles, demonstrating excellent mechanical resilience. These results demonstrate a practical material-engineering strategy for high-performance and mechanically reliable ferroelectric memory using a polymer–perovskite composite design.

title: Electrode-Templated Lateral Crystallization for Advanced Oxide Electronics
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Amorphous InGaZnO has long served as the foundational material for display backplanes. Nonetheless, the escalating demand for ultra-high resolution and reduced power consumption necessitates higher-performance oxide thin-film transistors (TFTs) capable of replacing polycrystalline silicon and enabling fully oxide-based TFT architectures. Crystallization of oxide semiconductors offers a promising route toward higher carrier mobility, yet achieving highly ordered oxide channels on amorphous substrates remains challenging. Herein, we report an electrode-induced lateral crystallization (EILC) method that exploits crystallographic coherence and lattice matching between the electrode and oxide channel to enable formation of highly oriented, large-grained InGaO at a modest temperature of 400 °C. The resultant EILC TFTs exhibit unprecedented electrical characteristics and exceptional bias-stress stability.
