However, existing polarity-engineering approaches often fail to preserve high-quality contact interfaces because atomically thin 2D semiconductors are highly sensitive to fabrication processes. Here, we introduce an effective buffer-layer removal process that enables polarity transformation while preserving a high-quality contact interface. A thin semimetal layer (Bi or Sb) is deposited prior to high-work-function metal evaporation and subsequently removed by a wet chemical treatment that preserves a high-quality metal/semiconductor interface. Minimizing the contact angle of the rinsing solution suppresses wrinkle and bubble formations and reduces Fermi-level pinning. The same WSe2 transistors transform from semimetal-dominated n-type transport before treatment to high-work-function-metal-dominated p-type transport afterward. Monolayer devices exhibit a maximum two-terminal hole field-effect mobility of 313 cm2 V–1 s–1 after treatment, while also supporting a maximum electron mobility of 41 cm2 V–1 s–1 before treatment. These results demonstrate n-to-p polarity transformation in WSe2 transistors enabled by a removable semimetal layer, providing a potential doping-free route toward complementary 2D electronics.

title: Hydrogen-Bond-Regulated PAN/PTFBZ Nanofibrous Composite Barriers for Flame-Resistant Thermal Runaway Protection
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Electrospun polymer barriers are attractive for lightweight thermal protection in compact lithium–ion battery (LIB) devices, but their limited flame resistance and structural stability under thermal abuse restrict their practical use. Herein, a hydrogen-bond-regulated nanofibrous composite barrier was developed by incorporating trifluoromethyl-modified benzoxazine (TFBZ)-derived components into a polyacrylonitrile (PAN) matrix. The benzoxazine-derived phenolic hydroxyl groups could interact with the nitrile groups of PAN through O–H···N≡C hydrogen bonding, contributing to improved interfacial compatibility and fibrous-network stabilization while retaining the processability of PAN. Thermogravimetric analysis showed that PAN/PTFBZ retained 96.1% of its mass at 300 °C, compared with 75.8% for pure PAN. Cone calorimetry showed that the total heat release and total smoke production were reduced by 64.9% and 45.1%, respectively, and the limiting oxygen index (LOI) increased from 18% to 31%. In battery-level thermal abuse tests, the time to complete thermal runaway (TR) increased from 1068.7 ± 14.6 s to 1884.7 ± 44.2 s, corresponding to 76.4% delay. These results suggest that interfacial hydrogen-bonding regulation, together with the ─CF3-modified benzoxazine-derived structure and compact char formation, contributes to improved flame resistance, structural retention, and battery-level thermal-abuse protection.

title: SERS-Active Nanocomposite Contact Lenses for Label-Free Multiplexed Biosensing of Tear Analytes
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Continuous monitoring remains limited by the fact that most wearable biosensors are built around single-analyte recognition chemistries, even though many physiological states are defined by changes across multiple metabolites. Tear fluid is one of the most biochemically informative biofluids accessible non-invasively, but contact lens biosensors have largely relied on enzymatic or electrochemical techniques that are difficult to extend beyond one target marker at a time. Here, we report a label-free surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy (SERS)-active contact lens in which gold nanostars are grown in situ on commercial hydrogel contact lenses. The resulting gold nanostar-loaded contact lens (AuNS-CL) introduces a plasmonic sensing layer directly onto the wearable substrate, with a substrate-averaged SERS enhancement factor of ∼105, while preserving the lens’ physiochemical properties. Quantitative biosensing was demonstrated using a digital thresholding method to account for variable hotspot distributions. Metabolites such as lactate and urea were quantified through their diagnostic bands in several solutions, including artificial tears and a mixture of tear analytes. The AuNS-CLs showed a strong linear response in the physiological range and recovery errors below 10%. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first demonstration of a wearable contact lens for label-free SERS quantification of tear metabolites.

title: A Keratin and Polyacrylamide Dual Network Hydrogel Based on Dynamic Coordination between Polydopamine and Mg2+ for Infected Wound Repair
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Exogenous bacterial infection severely impairs skin wound repair and creates a complex therapeutic challenge that requires simultaneous infection control, oxidative stress regulation, and tissue regeneration. In this study, a PAM/HK/PDANP-Mg2+ multifunctional hydrogel (HPPM) was developed as a cascade therapeutic dressing for infected wounds. In this system, polyacrylamide (PAM) provided a flexible covalently cross-linked framework. Hydrolyzed keratin (HK) offered bioactive and cytocompatible interfaces. Polydopamine nanoparticles (PDANPs) endowed the hydrogel with adhesiveness, photothermal antibacterial activity, and radical scavenging capacity. Coordination between Mg2+ and PDA, together with intermolecular hydrogen bonding, contributed to reversible physical cross-linking within the PAM framework. The optimized HPPM (0.012) hydrogel exhibited a porous structure, high swelling ratio (∼1277%), strong adhesion properties (31.00 kPa), and large tensile elongation (∼560%). Under 808 nm near-infrared (NIR) irradiation, HPPM achieved mild photothermal heating and over 99% antibacterial efficiency against Escherichia coli (E. coli) and Staphylococcus aureus (S. aureus). It also showed favorable antioxidant activity, cytocompatibility, and pro-migratory effects. In an S. aureus-infected rat wound model, HPPM (0.012) + NIR accelerated wound closure, reduced inflammation, enhanced collagen deposition and re-epithelialization, and regulated IL-10/TNF-α expression. These results suggest that HPPM promotes infected wound healing through dynamic coordination-driven cascade remodeling of the infected wound microenvironment.

title: Diffuse Fabry-Pérot Cavities from a Bifunctional Metal Mesh for Angle-Invariant Electrochromic Camouflage
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Tungsten trioxide (WO3) is a widely studied electrochromic material, yet its monochromatic switching behavior limits its applicability in scenarios requiring dynamic color modulation. To address this limitation, integration with a Fabry-Pérot (F-P) optical cavity has emerged as an effective strategy for expanding color tunability while reducing viewing-angle dependence. In this work, a simplified F-P cavity is constructed using stainless-steel mesh (SSM) as a bifunctional reflector and electrode, with a sputtered WO3 film serving as the electrochromic spacer. This design enables continuous full-spectrum color modulation across the visible range through precise regulation of the WO3 layer thickness. Meanwhile, the microscale topological roughness of the SSM introduces diffuse light scattering, which synergistically couples with F-P interference to compensate for optical path variations at different viewing angles. As a result, angle-independent structural coloration is achieved over a broad viewing-angle range from 15 to 90°. Furthermore, benefiting from the high electrical conductivity and unique porous structure of the SSM, a 14 cm × 14 cm inverted flexible electrochromic device was successfully fabricated. The resulting device exhibits fast switching kinetics, excellent mechanical durability under repeated bending, and stable reversible multicolor performance, demonstrating a scalable and cost-effective platform for adaptive visible-light camouflage and energy-efficient reflective display applications.

title: Porosity Tunable Silk Fibroin Microspheres Enhance Cartilage Repair in Rabbit Model
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Repairing articular cartilage defects is particularly challenging due to the tissue's hypovascularity and limited intrinsic healing capacity, which pose significant clinical challenges. Biomaterial-based scaffolds have shown promising outcomes in terms of repair capacity; however, finding a robust scaffold system remains challenging in cartilage tissue engineering. In this study, silk fibroin porous microspheres were fabricated using the co-axial electrospraying technique, followed by ethanol treatment to induce crosslinking and enhance microsphere stability. Interestingly, we observed that while changing the ethanol concentration from 100% to 75% to crosslink the silk microsphere resulted in the formation of tunable micropores, with pore sizes up to 87 μm in nonporous microspheres and ranging from 80–200 μm in porous microspheres. Then, we seeded human adipose-derived mesenchymal stem cells (hAdMSCs) onto microspheres to evaluate cell adhesion and proliferation over time. The microspheres exhibited enhanced cell adhesion during in vitro cytocompatibility assessments. Notably, porous microspheres displayed superior cell migration compared to nonporous microspheres, attributed to their interconnected pore architecture. Additionally, hAdMSCs-laden microspheres were further studied for their chondrogenic potential under induction conditions, demonstrating cartilage-specific marker expression. Moreover, macroscopic observations and histological staining images showed cartilage regeneration in a rabbit cartilage-defect model, in which porous microspheres outperformed nonporous counterparts due to their enhanced nutrient transfer and host-scaffold integration. Together, these results suggest that silk fibroin microspheres can mimic the extracellular matrix microenvironment, support cell growth, and promote matrix accumulation for effective cartilage repair.

title: Two-stage robust coordinated scheduling of port integrated energy systems for resilience enhancement with flexible resource collaboration

Diffusion Models for Small-Molecule Design
abstract: Abstract Diffusion models (DMs) have emerged as a class of generative models for controllable small-molecule design in drug discovery capable of progressively transforming noisy or partially specified molecular states into candidate structures under structural, geometric, and property constraints. This Review provides a comprehensive overview of the methodological foundations and representative applications of diffusion-based molecular generation, emphasizing the alignment among molecular representations, generative dynamics, controllable design, and evaluation and validation. Particular attention is given to recent advances in property- and structure-guided generation, target-aware and fragment-based design, multiobjective optimization, and synthesis-aware generation. We also discuss the roles of data sets, computational evaluation, and prospective experiments in assessing the chemical and biological relevance of generated molecules. By organizing these developments within a unified conceptual framework, we provide computational chemists and drug discovery researchers with a structured roadmap that balances the mathematical rigor with chemical intuition. Throughout, we highlight current methodological limitations and unresolved challenges and conclude with future directions toward chemically credible and experimentally grounded molecular design. To facilitate navigation of this rapidly evolving field, we introduce an interactive companion platform (https://diffsmd.scbdd.com) that provides a curated, continuously updated repository of model architectures and visualizations.

title: Data center cooling in the AI era: cross-scale challenges and system-level outlook
abstract: The rapid growth of artificial intelligence (AI) is fundamentally reshaping data center thermal and energy requirements, driven by increasing power densities and heterogeneous workload characteristics. This review provides an integrated cross-scale and temporal perspective that connects AI heat generation with chip-, rack-, and facility-scale thermal management and their interactions with external energy, water, and grid infrastructures. Modern AI workloads, enabled by accelerator-based hardware, can generate highly localized and temporally dynamic heat fluxes, challenging traditional assumptions of uniform and steady-state cooling design. Accordingly, a range of cooling technologies is examined, including air-based systems, liquid cooling approaches, hybrid configurations, and heat-reuse strategies, with emphasis on their performance limits and deployment constraints. The analysis further identifies key cross-cutting barriers to scalability and efficiency, including thermodynamic irreversibility, coupled water–energy–grid dependencies, cross-scale thermal interactions, reliability and maintainability constraints, and technology-specific trade-offs. Building on these observations, future cooling systems are expected to shift toward integrated and adaptive designs that prioritize multi-objective optimization rather than isolated performance improvements. Emerging directions include grid-responsive and water-aware operation, thermal storage-enabled temporal decoupling, co-designed computing and cooling infrastructures, and predictive closed-loop thermal management enabled by digital twins and data-driven control. Collectively, the findings highlight a transition from component-level optimization toward fully integrated system architectures that jointly optimize energy efficiency, resource utilization, operational resilience, and computational performance across spatial and temporal scales.

title: Conformational inversion mediated organic crystal actuator with extended stroke, self-healing, and optical switching
abstract: Dynamic molecular crystals with the capability to effectively convert thermal energy into mechanical work offer a compelling platform for microactuators. However, developing crystalline actuation materials that simultaneously achieve large and reversible deformation, rapid response, robust cyclability, and integrated optoelectronic functionality remains a formidable challenge. Herein, we take advantage of the conformational inversion of cyclohexyl groups and have rationally developed a dynamic organic crystal based on a dibenzothiophene sulfone derivative, BcDT, which exhibits exceptionally large, rapid, and reversible elongation. The thermally induced chair-to-boat conformational inversion of the introduced cyclohexyl moieties drives a cooperative phase transition that yields a linear elongation of ~14.3% along the crystal long axis, which delivers a work density of ~6.8 × 102 J m−3 and an efficiency of ~0.014%. Notably, the crystal features an uncommon self-healing capability, autonomously repairing macroscopic cracks during heating/cooling stages, ensuring its structural integrity and reliable actuation over multiple thermal cycles. The phase transition also enables reversible switching of linear and nonlinear optical properties, including a 4.2-fold modulation of two-photon excited fluorescence and tunable polarization anisotropy. Leveraging these properties, we demonstrate that BcDT crystals can function as microactuator devices to propel a heavy object and cooperatively lift a platform. This work establishes a molecular design strategy that integrates rapid, high-stroke actuation, self-healing, and optical switching within a single crystalline system, overcoming key functional limitations of current microactuators based on dynamic molecular crystals.

title: Rippled graphene pores as fluidic memristive devices with synaptic and neuromorphic functionalities
abstract: Nanofluidic memristive devices work with nanoscale pores (or channels) and ions dissolved in water, which harness the ionic memory effect aiming to store and process information. These devices share the same charge carriers as biological systems and bring hope for better emulating the neural functions and developing ionic circuits for neuromorphic applications. Specifically, theory and experiments suggest that nanoconfinement is essential for inducing a memory effect, which places a limit on the pore size to nm-scale or smaller. Such devices are, however, difficult to scale up with precision and operate with long-term stability. Here, we show that a micrometer size pore, generally expected to exhibit a linear ion transport, can display a pronounced memory effect, if its rim is wrapped by strongly curved and tightly stacked graphene. We attribute the observation to slow ion dynamics confined in the rippled graphene edges. The devices are easy to scale up and integrate into fluidic circuits. The memory effect is ion-selective and, crucially, exhibits long endurance, which enables reversible modification of the conductance states using programmable voltage spikes and various electrolytes over a long time, akin to biological synaptic plasticity. Thanks to this plasticity, our devices and their integrated circuits enable storing, transmitting and processing information with exceptionally high reliability, fidelity and accuracy, as evidenced by the effective processing of largescale and event-based information in the identification of both grayscale and color images, and in the real-time analysis of emulated neural signals. Our results highlight nanoscale morphology of the pore wall as an important parameter regulating ion transport, in addition to the well-documented pore’s charge and size, and indicate that the stringent nanoconfinement for ionic memory can be lifted from restricting the pore size to designing its rim structure. The devices and their integrated circuits may find use in ionic neuromorphic applications.

title: Promoting photocatalytic methane oxidative coupling via gradient oxidation field engineering
abstract: The efficient and selective photocatalytic oxidative coupling of methane (OCM) into valuable chemicals remains an unresolved challenge in modern science. Herein, we report the design and synthesis of a robust photocatalyst by constructing photocatalytic gradient oxidation field on mesoporous TiO2, which demonstrates exceptional OCM performance and outperforms other benchmark photocatalysts. The optimized photocatalytic system exhibits a high CH4 conversion rate of 1.2 mmol h−1, a high C2 hydrocarbon space-time yield of 82.7 mmol g−1 h−1 and 90.1% C2 selectivity, accompanied by a remarkable apparent quantum efficiency of over 11.6%. Mechanism analyses reveal that the gradient oxidation field introduced by the Au nanoislands and Pd atomic satellites can optimize the oxidation activity and selectivity with hydroxide and superoxide radicals, respectively. The synergistic interaction between the Au and Pd sites facilitates favorable adsorption of O2/CH4 reactants and promotes fast desorption of the C2H6 product, thereby accelerating the overall OCM process. This work demonstrates the critical role of photocatalytic oxidation field, and opens a new avenue for developing efficient and selective catalysts for various photocatalytic applications.

title: Faster global mid-depth ocean connectivity in observations
abstract: Ocean circulation redistributes heat, carbon, and biogeochemical tracers through transport pathways connecting distant ocean regions, yet global connectivity of mid-depth transport pathways remains poorly constrained by observations. Here we establish an observational benchmark of global mid-depth water-mass connectivity, using more than 1.3 million displacements recorded by 9,920 Argo floats over the past two decades. The benchmark reveals that observed connectivity is generally faster than simulated, with mean connectivity timescales 23-29% shorter in the real ocean. This systematic discrepancy between observed and simulated mid-depth ocean connectivity arises from overestimated turnover timescales within subtropical gyre interiors and underrepresentation of rapid inter-basin exchanges along equatorial and western boundary pathways in the simulation-derived networks, particularly in the South Pacific and South Atlantic. These findings provide quantitative constraints on ocean interior transport, with broad implications for estimates of climate memory, tracer age, carbon sequestration, and marine biogeographic connectivity.

abstract: Chiral helical superstructures provide a platform to control photon polarization and electron spin, yet they are challenging to construct using inorganic materials. Now, homochiral triple helices that exhibit pronounced circularly polarized luminescence have been assembled from gold by tailoring the steric and stereochemical properties of supporting chiral cyclic ligands.

title: Characterizing Fill Factor Limitations in Perovskite‐Silicon Tandem Solar Cells
abstract: ABSTRACT Monolithic perovskite‐silicon tandem solar cells have achieved power conversion efficiencies approaching 35%. However, a significant gap remains to their thermodynamic limit, primarily due to fill factor ( FF ) losses. This work presents a methodology to identify the underlying mechanisms of the losses. Electroluminescence characterization reveals the potential FF without series resistance losses but cannot fully explain the observed FF limitations. An additional loss mechanism is the photoshunt, a phenomenon which the parallel shunt resistance apparently reduces under illumination in perovskite solar cells. Using an analytical model, we show that the photoshunt originates from competition between charge extraction, governed by transport‐layer properties and electric field, and recombination in the absorber and at interfaces. An equivalent circuit model quantifies its impact on subcell and tandem FF . Additionally, the two‐diode property of the Si subcell can also influence the tandem FF losses. Measurements on tandem devices under spectrally independent LED illumination show that photoshunt losses can be hidden under bottom‐cell‐limited conditions, explaining the preference for slightly bottom‐cell‐limited tandem designs. Reducing the photoshunt through improved charge transport and reduced recombination could enable operation closer to current matching while minimizing FF and efficiency losses.

title: Competitive Solvation Structure in a Deep Eutectic Electrolyte Enables High‐Voltage LiCoO 2 ‐Based Pouch Cells With 5000‐Cycle Stability
abstract: ABSTRACT Anion‐rich solvation structures improve interfacial stability but often impede Li + desolvation, limiting fast‐charging and low‐temperature performance in high‐voltage lithium metal batteries. Unlike conventional high‐concentration or weakly solvating electrolytes, we propose a deep eutectic electrolyte (DEE) using succinonitrile (SN) and dimethyl sulfone (MSM) with competitive coordination capability. This design shifts the Li + solvation from aggregate clusters (AGGs) to a balanced AGGs/contact ion pairs (CIPs) distribution, which lowers the Li + desolvation energy barrier, enhances the transport kinetics, and endows the DEE with an ionic conductivity of 3.87 mS cm −1 and a Li + transference number of 0.81. MSM moderates excessive SN coordination, suppressing parasitic reactions on the anode, thereby enabling stable Li plating/stripping for 6800 h. A lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide (LiTFSI)/lithium difluoro(oxalato)borate (LiDFOB) dual‐salt system further optimizes interfacial chemistry, yielding a bilayer solid electrolyte interphase comprising an inorganic‐rich inner layer and a flexible organic outer layer. LiCoO 2 ||Li cells retain 97.1% capacity after 1000 cycles at 5C (3.0–4.5 V) and operate stably at −10°C. A 3.0 Ah LiCoO 2 ||Li pouch cell further delivers a high energy density of 417 Wh kg −1 , and LiCoO 2 ||graphite pouch cells sustain long‐term durability over 5000 cycles. This competitive solvation strategy effectively harmonizes kinetics and interfacial robustness for high‐voltage, fast‐charging DEEs.

title: Bioprinting, ten years on: from shape to function
abstract: Bioprinting has moved from building organ-like shapes that keep cells alive to constructs judged by function. However, function only emerges when computational design, printing hardware and instructive bioinks are coupled in one process. Making this coupling routine and reproducible is essential for translating printed tissues into credible therapies and models.

title: Nonlinear Kinetic Optimization via Strong–Weak Cosolvent Synergy in Aqueous Zinc Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT Cosolvent engineering for aqueous Zn metal batteries has traditionally emphasized thermodynamic stabilization, whereas the kinetic dimension of Zn 2+ charge transfer—particularly in multi‐cosolvent systems—remains far less understood. Here we conduct a systematic study on a dual‐cosolvent electrolyte pairing a strong cosolvent (DMSO) with a weak cosolvent (DMC). Through spatial decoupling, the strong cosolvent directly coordinates to stabilize the primary solvation shell, while the weak cosolvent forms a dynamic outer‐shell buffer. This unique context modulates Zn–ligand binding, facilitates desolvation, and guides the formation of a regulated SEI. Consequently, this architecture preserves comparably high thermodynamic stability while unlocking a nonlinear kinetic optimization exclusive to the dual‐cosolvent regime. Using a multi‐descriptor framework, we demonstrate a ∼40% reduction in the charge‐transfer barrier relative to single‐cosolvent systems. This kinetic enhancement translates into robust practical performance, establishing strong–weak cosolvent synergy as a versatile design principle for next‐generation aqueous batteries.

title: Synergistic Surface‐Bulk Induction of Uniform Out‐of‐Plane (100) Orientation for High‐Efficiency Perovskite Solar Cells
abstract: ABSTRACT Perovskite thin films featuring out‐of‐plane oriented (100) crystallographic facets are pivotal for advancing the efficiency and stability of perovskite solar cells, owing to their superior charge transport properties and reduced deep‐level defect density. However, conventional single‐strategy modification approaches are typically constrained by limited control over crystal orientation and spatially heterogeneous orientation distribution, hindering the full exploitation of such beneficial facets. Herein, we present a surface‐bulk synergistic induction strategy that overcomes the limitations of single modification approaches, effectively promoting directional grain alignment and cooperatively guiding ordered out‐of‐plane growth during thermal annealing. Benefiting from the successful fabrication of a perovskite film with a uniform and predominant preferred orientation, the inverted perovskite solar cells achieve a champion power conversion efficiency of 26.98% (certified 26.41%). Furthermore, the homogeneous texture and high intrinsic stability of the (100) facets enable the devices to retain 93.5% of their initial PCE after 1000 h of operational stability testing. This strategy effectively tackles the technical constraints of precursor solution regulation and solid‐state surface treatment, offering a novel research model for the precise modulation of perovskite thin film crystal facets and the secondary growth of polycrystalline thin films.

title: Lumped Circuits Modeling of Dynamic Energy Transfer in Triboelectric Nanogenerators with Nonlinear Electromechanical Coupling
abstract: ABSTRACT Powering autonomous electronics, sensors, and wearable systems using small‐scale daily mechanical energy is becoming increasingly important. Triboelectric nanogenerators (TENGs) offer a lightweight, flexible, and adaptable route for such applications, particularly when movements are involved. Here, we present a first‐of‐its‐kind unified dynamic energy‐transfer framework for TENGs, coupling their mechanical and electrical domains through a lumped element‐based equivalent circuit (LEEC) model. The framework captures time‐varying electrostatic behavior and key mechanical parameters, mass, damping, and stiffness, within a single predictive platform, enabling system‐level analysis of dynamic efficiency, impedance, resonance, and power transfer under different excitation conditions. The Thévenin equivalent model reveals that TENG performance is dynamically governed by excitation frequency, resonance, load matching, and surface charge density, approaching a time‐averaged theoretical efficiency of ∼54%. Experimental validation across devices with varied mechanical parameters shows close agreement with theory in electrical response and frequency‐dependent behavior. Furthermore, four borophene‐modified TENGs with different charge‐generation characteristics exhibit a systematic increase in electrical output and an estimated efficiency of up to 14.2% for the examined parameter space, supporting the model‐predicted dependence of energy‐conversion performance on surface charge density. The LEEC‐guided platform enables coupled energy and information harvesting through resonance‐enhanced capacitor charging and self‐powered road‐state sensing.

title: Dual Metal Dopants Advance Near‐Room‐Temperature PbS‐based Thermoelectrics
abstract: ABSTRACT Low‐cost lead sulfide (PbS) exhibits poor near‐room‐temperature (300–573 K) thermoelectric performance, limiting its practical applications. Here, Se/Te alloying coupled with dual‐metal Zn/Ge co‐doping is employed to enhance the near‐room‐temperature thermoelectric performance of n‐type PbS. Se/Te alloying forms a single‐phase PbS 0.5 Se 0.35 Te 0.15 solid solution (PbS(Se/Te)), where alloy‐induced mass and strain fluctuations enhance phonon scattering, reducing the lattice thermal conductivity from ∼2.09 W m −1 K −1 for PbS to ∼0.75 W m −1 K −1 at 300 K without compromising electrical transport. Zn/Ge co‐doping further optimizes carrier transport by regulating lattice defects and tuning carrier density, achieving a high carrier mobility of ∼522 cm 2 V −1 s −1 and an optimized carrier density of ∼1.03 × 10 19 cm −3 . The optimized PbS(Se/Te)+0.6‰Zn+5‰Ge sample exhibits an enhanced power factor of ∼20.23 µW cm −1 K −2 at 300 K, yielding a ZT of ∼0.54 at 300 K and an average ZT of ∼0.80 over 300–573 K. A seven‐pair thermoelectric module achieves a maximum temperature difference (Δ T max ) of ∼33.4 K at T h = 343 K, and a single‐leg device reaches a peak conversion efficiency of ∼7.2% under a temperature difference of 300 K. These results highlight the potential of Zn/Ge co‐doping for advancing n‐type PbS‐based materials toward near‐room‐temperature cooling and low‐grade heat recovery.

title: Polymer‐Directed Crystal Growth Regulation: Template‐Free Synthesis of Mesoporous Single‐Crystalline Mn 2 OBO 3
abstract: ABSTRACT Transition metal borates are attractive anode candidates for lithium‐ion batteries (LIBs) because of their high specific capacity and environmental benignity; however, their structural collapse induced by large volume changes during cycling leads to rapid capacity degradation. In this study, we report a polymer‐directed crystal growth regulation strategy that enables the template‐free synthesis of mesoporous single‐crystalline Mn 2 OBO 3 (MSC Mn 2 OBO 3 ). Polyethyleneimine (PEI) acts as a bifunctional regulator, coordinating Mn 2+ ions and hydrogen bonding with borate ions to modulate hydrolysis and condensation, thereby yielding a hybrid precursor. Subsequent hydrothermal treatment yields single‐crystalline MnBO 2 OH nanobelts, which are converted by calcination into MSC Mn 2 OBO 3 . As an anode active material for lithium‐ion batteries, MSC Mn 2 OBO 3 delivers a reversible capacity of 1440 mAh g −1 at 0.2 A g −1 , more than twice that of bulk Mn 2 OBO 3 . Notably, this polymer‐directed strategy is readily extendable to doped MSC Mn 2 OBO 3 (e.g., Fe, V, and Mg), providing a versatile platform for the design of porous single‐crystalline materials for energy storage.

title: Scalable Hydrogel‐Programmed Porous Photonic Cement for Passive Daytime Cooling
abstract: ABSTRACT Cement is among the most widely produced materials on Earth, yet its strong solar absorption causes building envelopes to act as heat sources, increasing cooling energy demand. Here, we structurally program cement hydration to transform conventional cementitious materials into passive cooling interfaces. Through hydrogel‐confined mineralization of cement clinker, we construct a robust, hierarchically porous calcium–silicate–hydrate (C–S–H) network that integrates broadband light scattering, vapor transport and thermal insulation. By regulating the composition and crystallinity of the hydrates, the material achieves ∼95% solar reflectance and ∼98% infrared emissivity without the use of additional photonic fillers. The hygroscopic nature of the network further enables sustained evaporative cooling under humid or cloudy conditions where radiative cooling alone becomes inefficient. Life‐cycle analysis indicates that this strategy provides a pathway to transform high‐emission cement into carbon‐mitigating materials integrated within opaque building envelopes, enabling the scalable deployment of daytime radiative cooling across the built environment.

title: In Situ Topological Dealloying Enables Atomically Coupled Metal‐Oxide Heterostructures
abstract: ABSTRACT Metal‐oxide heterostructures are central to energy conversion and electronic devices because interfaces can modulate the configuration coupling among charge, spin, and orbit. However, conventional synthesis routes suffer from structural incompatibility and weak coupling, which hinder the universal construction of atomically coupled metal‐oxide heterointerfaces. Here, we develop an in situ topological dealloying strategy to construct metal‐oxide heterostructures with atomically interconnected interfaces. This strategy can be broadly applied to perovskite, spinel, columbite, and vanadate oxides, which enables the spontaneous formation of high‐density magnetic nanoalloys embedded within dielectric oxide matrices. Direct nanoscale visualizations of electric and magnetic fields reveal the coexistence of interfacial charge polarization and vortex‐like spin textures. These emergent dielectric and magnetic behaviors arise from atomically interfacial hybridization that mediates strong charge–spin interactions. When integrated into flexible architectures, these heterostructures exhibit broadband GHz‐frequency absorption (effective absorption bandwidth up to 6.6 GHz at 3.0 mm), high efficiency, and rapid electromagnetic‐to‐thermal energy conversion under microwave irradiation. This work establishes a general route to engineer metal‐oxide heterostructures for functional applications.

title: Staged Network Evolution Enables In Situ Strengthening and On‐Demand Recyclability of Polyurethanes via Dynamic Sulfilimine–Urea Bonds
abstract: ABSTRACT Cross‐linked polymers exhibit exceptional mechanical robustness, dimensional stability, and chemical resistance arising from permanent covalent networks. However, it remains challenging to tune mechanical properties after curing and to decouple on‐demand recyclability from in‐use stability. Herein, we report a staged network evolution strategy based on dynamic sulfilimine–urea bonds to address these demands. The rapid room‐temperature addition of isocyanates to sulfilimines forms dynamic sulfilimine–urea linkages, affording a solvent‐resistant initial polyurethane (SUP‐S1). Subsequent thermal treatment of SUP‐S1 induces dissociation of the sulfilimine–urea linkages, regenerating the sulfilimine motifs and releasing isocyanates that are captured in situ by backbone hydroxyl groups to form thermodynamically stable urethane bonds. The tensile strength and toughness of the obtained polyurethane (SUP‐S2) are significantly enhanced, increasing from 17 to 42 MPa and from 55 to 158 MJ m −3 , respectively, while the Young's modulus is retained. Moreover, the photoclip of sulfilimine motifs facilitates on‐demand recyclability by reducing the cross‐link density. The resulting recyclable polyurethane (SUP‐S3) exhibits excellent multi‐recyclability, retaining over 96% of its mechanical properties after five recycling cycles. This staged network evolution design reconciles the enhancement of mechanical properties with end‐of‐life recyclability within a single material platform, providing a robust pathway for the development of next‐generation sustainable cross‐linked polymeric materials.

title: Intrinsically Stretchable Fully π‐Conjugated Polymer Films Enabled by Supramolecular Plasticized Micro‐Crosslinking‐Network for Flexible Polymer Light‐Emitting Diodes
abstract: ABSTRACT Stretchable fully π‐conjugated polymers (FπCPs) films with a fantastic optoelectronic property and outstanding deformation tolerance capacity, is a promising candidate for the fabrication of flexible optoelectronics devices. However, previous reported stretchable FπCPs films undergo irreversible chain slippage and alignment upon strain release, leading to plastic deformation, and consequently severe performance degradation during cyclic‐deformation operation. Herein, we proposed a supramolecular soft‐micro‐crosslinked strategy to achieve the stretchable p ‐ n FπCPs (P X ‐OXI 1‐X ‐HDI) films with a recoverable‐deformation ability for the flexible electronics. Three‐dimensional (3D) supramolecular micro‐crosslinked network formed by oxime‐urethane and hydrogen bonds allow for the excellent elastic deformation to dissipate transient stress while fundamentally suppressing permanent chain slippage. Micro‐crosslinked p ‐ n FπCPs free‐standing films achieved an elongation at break of > 40%. Flexible PLED based on P X ‐OXI 1‐X ‐HDI showed a stable green emission with brightness of ∼3300 cd cm −2 . Meanwhile, the performance of transferred PLED based on stretchable micro‐crosslinked films are independent on the tensile ratio (>20%) with a maximum brightness of ∼2000 cd m −2 , revealed the excellent cycle‐deformation‐stability than device based on crosslinked films. Therefore, these supramolecular micro‐crosslinked networks can enhance instantaneous toughness and confer a critical resistance to long‐term stress relaxation and plastic deformation, further ensure the device excellent deformation stability.

title: Intranasal Pathogenesis‐Adaptive Nanotherapeutics Reinstate Regenerative Competence for Post‐Stroke Neural Repair
abstract: ABSTRACT Poststroke neurorehabilitation is limited by the poor regenerative capacity of adult neurons. Although neural stem cells (NSCs) can generate new neurons, their reparative potential is constrained by inefficient delivery to cerebral lesions and a hostile regenerative niche. Here, analysis of a single‐nucleus transcriptomic dataset revealed pronounced dysfunction and intercellular crosstalk among neurons, microglia, and NSCs, highlighting redox imbalance and impaired nitric oxide (NO) signaling as potential therapeutic targets. Guided by these findings, we develop FCeO 2 @GLp, a pathogenesis‐adaptive nanotherapeutic integrating reactive oxygen species scavenging, NO replenishment and immune modulation within cerebral ischemic microenvironment. Following intranasal administration, FCeO 2 @GLp actively adheres to the olfactory epithelium (OE), reaches infarcted brain regions, releases cerium oxide (CeO 2 ) nanozyme, fingolimod, and a NO donor in response to local acidity. This coordinated strategy alleviates oxidative stress, reprograms microglia, protects neurons, and enhances NSC proliferation and neuronal differentiation. Consequently, FCeO 2 @GLp effectively reduces infarct volume and cerebral edema during the acute phase, and improves long‐term neurological function and survival, establishing a lesion‐responsive strategy for poststroke neural repair.

title: Deciphering Roles of Interfacial Tunable Primer for High Active Material Contents Pure Silicon Electrodes
abstract: Abstract While pure silicon (Si) is a highly attractive anode material for next‐generation high‐energy‐density lithium‐ion batteries, its practical implementation is limited by severe volumetric fluctuations during cycling. This intrinsic instability inevitably induces continuous structural degradation, strictly restricting the maximum allowable active material fraction within the electrode. To address this critical challenge, we design an interfacial tunable functional primer ( fp ) that serves as an effective multi‐component bridging agent. By optimizing the mechanical resilience and electrochemical cohesion among electrode components, the fp layer dissipates interfacial stress and secures continuous electron conduction pathways. Furthermore, the unique ionophoric properties of the benzoxazine framework directly regulate the interfacial solvation structure and enhance ion flux. Driven by these integrated effects, the fp ‐modified Si anode achieves remarkable electrochemical reversibility even at a nearly binder‐free composition containing 99 wt% active material content. This strategy completely averts the rapid physical degradation typically observed in standard binder networks under such extreme formulations. Furthermore, fp ‐modified Si demonstrates practical viability by assembling double‐stacked pouch cells paired with NCM90 cathodes, which exhibit long‐term cycle durability. This study provides a highly effective paradigm for electrode‐component regulation and molecular‐level engineering in pure Si anode interfacial modification strategies.

title: A Janus Bilayer Portland Cement‐Based Moisture‐Electricity Generator via Hydrogen‐Bonding Network Regulation
abstract: ABSTRACT The ubiquitous interaction between ambient moisture and built environments presents a compelling opportunity for continuous energy harvesting through moisture‐electricity generation (MEG). However, current MEG materials fail to satisfy high‐power demands in buildings because hydrogen bonds, indispensable for the structural integrity of soft carbon‐chain networks, severely restrict water diffusion, and thus bottleneck MEG performance. Hydrated Portland cement, featuring a robust silicate backbone, allows aggressive modulation of the water hydrogen‐bonding network (HBN), emerging as an ideal platform for higher performance. Here, we developed a Portland cement‐based moisture‐electricity generator (CMEG) via a facile asymmetric acid etching strategy, extending MEG to cementitious material systems. The resulting CMEG presents a Janus bilayer architecture with a stark gradient in hygroscopicity across the layers to drive the unidirectional diffusion of water molecules. Mechanistically, the etching process induces the breakage of HBN, which unlocks ultrafast water diffusion throughout the top layer and thus accelerates selective ion transport toward the bottom layer. Remarkably, CMEG delivers an extremely high short‐circuit current density of 723 µA/cm 2 and output power density of 112.5 µW/cm 2 . Furthermore, CMEG demonstrates exceptional scalability, modular integration capabilities and nearly identical mechanical strength to that before acid etching, proving its giant potential for future self‐powered buildings and infrastructures.

title: Determining Composition–Structure–Property Relationships in Quaternary Perovskitoids Through Megalibraries
abstract: ABSTRACT Understanding how composition governs structure and function is essential for designing functional materials, however, establishing these relationships remains prohibitively slow for materials with massive and tunable compositional spaces, such as Bi and Sb‐based perovskitoids. Here, a novel megalibrary‐based synthetic methodology has been developed and used to rapidly identify and characterize quaternary perovskite derivatives across an expansive compositional space. Parylene templates were used to synthesize one million compositionally distinct, positionally encoded Cs 3 Sb 2−x Bi x Br 9−y I y microcrystals on 2 × 2 cm 2 chips with 20 µm periodicity. These megalibraries enabled the systematic investigation of structural and optoelectronic evolution across this compositional space using micro‐area x‐ray diffraction, position‐resolved absorbance spectroscopy, scanning electron microscopy, and confocal fluorescence microscopy. An unusual non‐monotonic bandgap shift was observed with increasing Br content, reaching a minimum at 33% Br. This behavior is attributed to the formation of halide‐segregated heterostructures, consisting of low‐dimensional, I‐rich shells surrounding Br‐rich layered cores. Phase separation was most pronounced in Sb‐rich compositions, which were found to stabilize heterostructure formation. This study demonstrates how megalibraries enable the simultaneous evaluation of key optoelectronic parameters, including bandgap and phase purity, revealing complex, composition‐dependent structure‐function relationships in perovskitoids and providing a versatile platform for accelerating the discovery of optoelectronic‐relevant materials.

title: Efficient H 2 O 2 Photosynthesis With Valorization by X‐Packing NDI Cocrystal Catalyst
abstract: ABSTRACT Solar‐driven photocatalytic H 2 O 2 synthesis offers a sustainable and green alternative to the energy‐intensive anthraquinone process. However, coordinated regulation of electron‐transfer (ET) and energy‐transfer (EnT) pathways for efficient H 2 O 2 production remains challenging. Organic charge‐transfer (CT) cocrystals, which reconfigure the energy‐level structure through new intermolecular electronic states, provide a promising avenue to overcome this limitation. Herein, we report a CT cocrystal photocatalyst, DPNDI‐Py, prepared by liquid‐assisted grinding (LAG) of N, N′‐bis(4‐pyridyl)‐1,4,5,8‐naphthalenediimide (DPNDI) and pyrene (Py). The cocrystal harbors an X‐packed donor‐acceptor arrangement, with a crossing angle of 52° between the long axes of DPNDI and Py. Spectroscopic measurements confirm strong intermolecular CT, and transient spectroscopy supports CT‐related excited‐state dynamics and the formation of long‐lived triplet states, while theoretical calculations indicate electronic structure favorable for intersystem crossing (ISC). Mechanistic studies indicate that both EnT and ET pathways are utilized in photocatalysis. Under LED irradiation in air, DPNDI‐Py delivers an average H 2 O 2 production rate of 18.47 ± 0.57 mmol g −1 h −1 coupled with an 83.7 ± 2.26% dehydroascorbic acid (DHA) yield from ascorbic acid (AA) oxidation. This work provides mechanistic insight into CT‐mediated photocatalysis, offering a design principle for organic photocatalysts.

abstract: For years, researchers have studied people with a genetic predisposition to Alzheimer’s and other dementias. They might have even more to learn from those who don’t get the disease.

title: Author Correction: Heat treatment in an oxygen-rich environment to suppress deep-level traps in Cu2ZnSnS4 solar cell with 11.51% certified efficiency
Mesoscale Chiroptical Order in Achiral Metal-Halide Nanoplatelet Assemblies
source: ACS Energy Letters: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract This viewpoint presents the circular dichroism emerging directly from the self-assembly of achiral metal-halide perovskite nanoplatelets such as Cs3Cd2Cl7, Rb3Cd2Cl7, and CsPbBr3. Specifically, even when they form only short-range, polydisperse assemblies rather than the long-range helical superlattices reported in prior works, these short assemblies also exhibit chiral optical properties. The effect persists across emissive and nonemissive systems; with diverse stacking morphologies, and both in solution and film forms. Thus, this viewpoint establishes mesoscale chirality as a general principle of nanoplatelet self-assemblies.

title: Rational Selection of Hole Contacts with an Organic Light-Emitting Diode Industry p-Dopant for Fully Vacuum-Processed Perovskite/Silicon Tandems
source: ACS Energy Letters: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Translating perovskite/silicon tandems to fully vacuum-based manufacturing requires vacuum-compatible p-doped hole contacts, yet clear selection criteria for doped hole-transport materials (HTMs) remain underdeveloped compared with C60-based electron contacts. Here, we report a fully vacuum-processed perovskite/silicon tandem reaching 29.1% power conversion efficiency, among the highest reported for tandems with fully vacuum-deposited perovskite top cells, enabled by transferring the organic light-emitting diode (OLED)-industry p-dopant NDP-9 and an evaporable arylamine HTM into the perovskite stack. Comparing TaTm, Spiro-TTB, and TAPC shows that contact selection does not follow apparent host–dopant interaction strength derived from theoretical calculations or conventional optical, vibrational, and photoemission spectroscopies. Instead, device-level charge extraction and recombination metrics identify NDP-9-doped TaTm as the most effective contact, also yielding 20.0% in a single-junction 1.70 eV wide-bandgap cell. These results point to transport-based screening as a practical route to selecting vacuum-compatible doped hole contacts.

title: Operando Time-of-Flight Secondary Ion Mass Spectrometry Reveals Iodine-Mediated Redox Chemistry in Solid-State Li–S Batteries
source: ACS Energy Letters: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Understanding dynamic reaction pathways in all-solid-state batteries remains challenging because electrochemical processes occur at buried solid–solid interfaces and transient intermediates are difficult to detect with conventional analytical techniques. While operando techniques typically probe structural or macroscopic changes, direct detection of reactive species during operation remains experimentally demanding. Here, we introduce a dynamic operando time-of-flight secondary ion mass spectrometry platform that enables continuous chemical analysis of processes in a solid-state battery under electrochemical bias. Using this approach, we directly observe a pronounced increase of the I2– signal during charging of a Li–S composite cathode containing LiI, indicating the formation of elemental iodine. Concurrent changes in the sulfur-containing ion signals suggest the involvement of iodine species in the ongoing redox processes. These results reveal transient, low-concentration species at buried interfaces undetectable by other operando techniques, offering a pathway for identifying reactive intermediates in conversion-type solid-state batteries and related electrochemical systems.

title: Decoding Symmetry-Breaking Band Structures in Nanocatalysts for Kinetically Favorable Li-S Batteries
source: ACS Energy Letters: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The conventional d-band center theory represents catalyst electronic structures using an averaged energy and may therefore overlook higher-order information contained in the complex and asymmetric density of states of alloy catalysts (ACs). Here, combining quantum chemistry with interpretable machine learning, we identify the transformed d-band peak position (Epp) as an alternative electronic descriptor for alloy–polysulfide interactions in lithium-sulfur batteries. Epp integrates information related to the d-band position, bandwidth, and band shape, and correlates with the electron occupation of S3p–Md (M = metal) antibonding states and the calculated polysulfide adsorption strength. A series of bimetallic ACs recovered from spent lithium-ion batteries was employed to experimentally evaluate the descriptor. Within this series, CoFe shows favorable electrochemical performance, enabling an ampere-hour-level pouch cell with an energy density of 426 Wh kg–1 under a sulfur loading of 12.5 mg cm–2 and an electrolyte-to-sulfur ratio of 3.6 mL g–1.

title: Widespread North American pollution and health impacts from early twentieth century copper production
abstract: Mining and industrial emissions can be substantially reduced by technological interventions. The historical case of copper production in Anaconda, Montana shows the widespread health burdens that can result when lax regulation delays such interventions.

title: Agricultural data source choice as a dominant control on nitrogen surplus uncertainty
abstract:
Abstract
                  Agricultural nitrogen (N) surplus (the residual of total N inputs after harvest removal, plant-tissue storage, runoff and atmospheric losses) is a leading cause of groundwater and other environmental contamination in intensive food-producing regions, yet N surplus estimates often depend on inconsistent fertilizer, harvest and manure datasets in an N balance. Using California’s Central Valley as a data-rich test case, we propagate expert, survey-based, regulatory and county-level datasets through a fixed crop-specific N surplus framework to generate 24 cases. Holding model structure and land use constant, we quantify the large divergence in estimated N surplus arising from data choice, especially for manure-treated field crops. The uncertainty about N surplus is consequential: it can reorder which crops, regions and pathways receive priority for groundwater protection. The resulting spread among N surplus outcomes is large enough to alter hotspot rankings, mitigation priorities and screening-level estimates of economic burden. Credible nitrogen assessment at farm to global scales therefore requires explicit propagation of agricultural data source uncertainty, which can materially affect resulting N surplus estimates. Absent specific local data, the uncertainty magnitudes reported here may guide N surplus uncertainty assessment in other regional, national and global analyses.

title: Coal power lives longer next to data centres

abstract: Scientific grounds for a net-zero policy assume near-zero committed warming over a few decades after CO2 emissions cease. A modelling study suggests that if prior peak temperatures rise above 2 °C before cessation of CO2 emissions, committed warming increases, making it harder to stabilize global warming.

title: A further acceleration of clean energy is needed for global CO2 emissions to peak and decline
abstract:
Abstract

Here we project a decrease of 0.4% in 2026, probably as a short-term response to the energy shock triggered by the Iran conflict. title: Early evidence links data centre exposure to coal power retirement timelines
abstract: Data centre expansion may slow the coal-fired power plants phase-out, complicating decarbonization pathways. This study finds that coal units exposed to post-2020 data centres have lower retirement risks and their potential lifetime extensions could cause large additional CO2 emissions.

title: Synthesis of Hetero‐Dimensional Mechanically Interlocked Networks
abstract: ABSTRACT Mechanically interlocked polymer networks feature non‐covalent topological constraints between chains, in which the sliding of rings along axles allows adaptive deformation and energy dissipation. Yet these interlocking sites cannot cooperate, and the lack of direct stress transfer pathways between them leads to localized stress concentration at the chain level. Here, we report the synthesis of hetero‐dimensional mechanically interlocked networks (HDMINs), in which nanoporous two‐dimensional molecular sheets serve as multi‐threading platforms, each rigid sheet coupling its threaded chains into one cooperative network. One‐dimensional chains threaded through two‐dimensional polyaramid sheets in solution are captured by covalent crosslinking into a 2D/3D architecture. The mechanical bonds are preserved in this interlocking network, and their sheet‐coordinated sliding relieves local stress concentration and enhances energy dissipation. HDMINs are simultaneously stiffer, stronger and tougher than their non‐interlocked counterparts, showing that elevating the dimensionality of interlocking components converts discrete mechanical bonds into a cooperative network that bears load collectively.

title: Constructing Low‐Friction Ion Transport Pathways in Crosslinked Polymer Electrolyte for Practical Quasi‐Solid‐State Lithium Metal Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT Quasi‐solid‐state polymer electrolytes are promising candidates for lithium metal batteries (LMBs) with high energy density, but still suffer from sacrificed ionic conductivity caused by electrolyte solidification. Here, by tuning monomer structures with different Li + ‐affinity, we investigate the decisive role of the segmental solvation ability of the polymer matrix in cation transport. Owing to the overly strong affinity for cations, conventional ether segments significantly decrease the Li + relaxation rate, and the resulting “sticky” polymer chains impede Li + migration. In contrast, the weakly coordinating segments such as fluorinated ether could effectively minimize coupling with Li + ions, thereby constructing “low‐friction” cation transport pathways in crosslinked polymer electrolytes, as reflected by the nearly unchanged Li + relaxation kinetics and high ionic conductivity. Therefore, the industrial Li metal pouch cells achieve excellent comprehensive electrochemical performance under harsh lean‐electrolyte conditions, with electrolyte dosage even as low as 1.3 g Ah −1 . The 2 Ah NCM811/Li cell exhibits an extended lifespan beyond 520 cycles and maintains stable operation across a wide temperature range from −50°C to +90°C. The 8.7 Ah NCM955/Li cell delivers 550 Wh kg −1 energy density and demonstrates impressive cycling stability over 260 cycles. This work could inspire fundamental understanding and further development toward practical LMBs.

title: Bridge‐Level Electronic Compensation in Prussian White Cathodes: Charge‐Transfer Kinetic Regimes and Design Principles
abstract: ABSTRACT Prussian White (PW) cathodes are promising sodium–ion battery materials because of their open framework, low cost, and high structural reversibility. However, polarization and capacity loss under high‐rate or low‐temperature operation arise from coupled ionic, structural, interfacial, and electronic processes that are not fully captured by Na + diffusion or average structural evolution alone. This perspective introduces a bridge‐level electronic‐compensation framework in which the Fe─C≡N─TM bridge is treated as a local unit for describing local charge redistribution. Using Marcus‐type descriptors together with concepts of metal‐to‐metal charge transfer, intervalence charge transfer, and metal–ligand interactions, three physical contributions are emphasized: the local charge‐state free‐energy difference ( ΔG° ), cyanide‐mediated electronic coupling ( H ab ), and structure‐coupled reorganization energy ( λ ). Local bridge states are organized into descriptor‐based kinetic regimes based on the balance among energetic mismatch, electronic coupling, and structural reorganization, with transition‐metal chemistries serving as representative mechanistic cases. These descriptors are further translated into design principles involving redox‐level alignment, cyanide‐mediated coupling and network connectivity, and control of local structural reorganization. This perspective provides a physical basis for interpreting bridge‐level electronic compensation and considering how local energetic alignment, coupling, and structural reorganization can be regulated in PW cathodes.

title: An Engineered Thio‐Amino Polymer Achieves Potent, Safe, and Broad Cell Type Delivery in the Lung Mapped by Spatial Transcriptomics
abstract: ABSTRACT Efficient delivery of nucleic acids to the lung has the potential to impact future respiratory treatments. Current formulations exhibit significant limitations, including insufficient potency, single‐cell delivery characterizations, efficacy demonstrations in disease models, and toxicology assessments. Here we describe polymer 81 (P81), which, when used with hypotonic solvents, is 34.1‐ to 77.8‐fold more potent than previous polymers with various cargos for lung transfection by nebulized mRNA. Through the exploration of multiple routes of administration, P81 demonstrated a wide of range of cell‐type delivery, including bronchial airway epithelial cells, tracheal basal stem cells, and 54% of all cells in the distal lung, assessed via single‐cell spatial transcriptomics. Robust expression of mRNA‐encoded antibodies in the lung by P81 enabled quantification of target protein and successful suppression of SARS‐CoV‐2 infection. The toxicology assessments of multiple doses of P81 polyplexes via nebulization in rodents were unremarkable. Overall, P81 represents a step forward for inhaled nucleic acid delivery to the respiratory tract, positioning itself as an efficient, safe, and translatable delivery formulation.

title: A Coaxial Bioprinted Hydrogel With Semipermeable Sheath and Pro‐Chondrogenic Core for Articular Cartilage Repair
abstract: ABSTRACT Stem cell‐laden hydrogels represent a promising strategy for the functional repair of articular cartilage defects. However, the pathological joint microenvironment is often characterized by persistently elevated levels of pro‐inflammatory cytokines, which severely compromise transplanted cell survival and impair their chondrogenic differentiation potential. Inspired by the hierarchical mechanical gradient of native cartilage, we developed a sheath‐core biomimetic hydrogel (SC GAE ) via embedded coaxial bioprinting, featuring a robust poly(ethylene glycol)‐alginate (PA) sheath that spatially integrates mechanical support and immunoprotection around a soft, bioactive gelatin methacryloyl‐alginate‐decellularized extracellular matrix (GAE) core. The dense PA sheath provides immediate mechanical support and functions as a size‐selective diffusion barrier, permitting nutrient and oxygen permeation while effectively blocking inflammatory cytokines (>40 kDa). This protective niche enables the pericellular matrix‐mimicking GAE core to maintain stem cell viability >89% under pro‐inflammatory conditions and support robust chondrogenic differentiation. In a rabbit osteochondral defect model, bone marrow stromal cell‐laden SC GAE constructs promoted substantial cartilage repair, achieving defect filling, host integration, and regeneration of glycosaminoglycan‐rich hyaline‐like cartilage. This sheath‐core architecture design spatially integrates structural, mechanical, and immunoprotection functions, presenting a promising platform for the regeneration of load‐bearing articular cartilage.

title: VAMP725 and VAMP726 interact with cellulose synthase to support secondary cell wall formation
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
abstract: The formation of plant cell walls underpins morphogenesis, growth, and development of all plants. Cellulose is an essential and load-bearing cell wall polymer that is synthesized by Cellulose Synthase (CESA) protein complexes at the plasma membrane. In this study, we reveal that SNARE proteins Vesicle Associated Membrane Protein 726 (VAMP726) and VAMP725 associate with multiple CESA proteins. Consistent with these results, the VAMP726 is codelivered with the CESA proteins to the plasma membrane, and the proteins colocalize at intracellular compartments. We further show that the VAMPs, especially VAMP726, are important for CESA trafficking and sustenance of cellulose synthesis both in growing tissues and in secondary wall producing maturing tissues. Taken together, our study outlines an important intracellular process whereby VAMP proteins facilitate trafficking of CESA complexes during cellulose synthesis.

title: Host infection selects for sRNA variants that drive bacterial social cheating
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
abstract: Single-nucleotide mutations in regulatory small RNAs (sRNAs) represent a largely unexplored route to social cheating during bacterial infection. Here we show that arcZ , encoding a conserved Hfq-dependent sRNA in the plant pathogen Dickeya solani , undergoes recurrent single-nucleotide mutations during potato tuber infection. Five distinct arcZ alleles define a graded series of ArcZ functional impairment in which antifungal and protease activities are progressively reduced while virulence is compromised only in a subset of alleles. All five variants gain a fitness advantage exclusively during coinfection with wild-type arcZ 1 cells. This advantage is strongest when variants are rare and declines as cheater frequency increases, ultimately correlating with reduced total bacterial productivity, the canonical signature of social cheating and a tragedy of the commons. No fitness benefit is detected in vitro . Transcriptomic profiling of five arcZ variants identifies a conserved core of 186 downregulated genes enriched in secreted and diffusible functions. Systematic genetic dissection, supported by quantitative proteomics, establishes BudAB-dependent limitation of tissue acidification as the dominant cooperative public good exploited during infection. Wild-type arcZ 1 cells divert pyruvate flux toward acetoin via the BudAB pathway, maintaining a less acidic tissue environment that sustains disease progression; arcZ variants, which show reduced expression of this pathway, benefit from the less acidic environment maintained by wild-type cells without contributing to it. These results establish pleiotropic regulatory sRNAs as a previously unrecognized class of mutational targets for the emergence of social cheaters during host infection.

title: RNA and proteins joined up at the origins of life: Persistence is the point
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
abstract: What drove nucleic acids (NA) into functional associations with proteins (PR) at the origins of life? We reason from polymer physics and the Central Dogma that the fitness value of cooperating through a division of labor—NA for replication fidelity and PR for functional fitness—is much higher than for either polymer alone. Our model shows a Pareto Front, where NA and PR can bootstrap each other to achieve autocatalytic cooperativity toward biology.

title: A trefoil knot mimic and multiple pore states define the mechanism of a split-shell Tc toxin
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
abstract: Toxin complex (Tc) toxins are among the largest virulence factors secreted by pathogenic bacteria, operating via a sophisticated injection mechanism that translocates cytotoxic effectors into host cells. While most structural and mechanistic studies have focused on fused-shell Tc toxins such as PTC3 from Photorhabdus luminescens , the structurally distinct split-shell toxins remain poorly understood. Here we report cryoelectron microscopy structures of the split-shell Yersinia entomophaga Tc holotoxin (YenTc) in multiple conformational states at resolutions of 2.6 to 3.7 Å. We show that the chitinase subunit YenChi2 is essential for shell expression and stabilizes the N terminus of the shell subunit YenA1 in the prepore state. Our structures also reveal the first trefoil knot mimic in Tc toxins, which serves the dual function of stabilizing the linker domain and holding the two halves of the split shell together. We further describe three distinct pore states: the conventional pore state, an inverted pore state in which the shell rotates 180° around a hinge in YenA2, and a lollipop pore state induced at alkaline pH in which the YenA1-YenChi2 subcomplex fully dissociates from the channel. Strikingly, all three pore states also manifest in the TcA pentamer of P. luminescens PTC3, indicating that they represent a general but previously undescribed feature of Tc toxin pore formation. Taken together, our results establish a mechanistic framework for split-shell Tc toxins and expose a dynamic, multilevel intoxication pathway that may apply broadly to Tc toxins.

title: The highly heat-inducible HspA6 and the thermolabile DnaJB5 are potent regulators of heat shock transcription factor 1 activity
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
abstract: In response to proteotoxic stress the central regulator of the heat shock response (HSR) in mammalian cells, Hsf1, trimerizes, binds DNA, and drives transcription of heat shock genes. We previously showed that Hsc70 (HspA8) assisted by its J-domain protein (JDP) cochaperone DnaJB1 dissociates Hsf1 from DNA by monomerizing the trimeric Hsf1 and thereby attenuates the HSR. Whether this feedback mechanism is specific to the HspA8–DnaJB1 pair or instead reflects a broader, isoform- and JDP-selective Hsp70 network controlling Hsf1 remained unresolved. Here, we demonstrate that of all cytonuclear Hsp70s the highly heat-inducible HspA6 is most efficient in monomerizing Hsf1 in the presence of DnaJB1 and of all cytonuclear class A and class B JDPs, only DnaJB1, DnaJB4, and DnaJB5 assist in Hsf1 monomerization. Whereas cooperation of HspA6 and HspA8 with DnaJB1 and DnaJB4 absolutely depends on Hsp70s’ C-terminal glutamate-glutamate-valine-glutamate (EEVD)-motif, cooperation with DnaJB5 does not. Consistent with these data, overproduction of EEVD-deleted HspA8 and HspA6 down-regulate the HSR in HeLa cells. DnaJB5 knockdown reduces HspA8–Hsf1 interaction under nonstress conditions revealing DnaJB5 as major targeting factor for HspA8 binding to Hsf1. On temperature upshift DnaJB5 partially unfolds and partitions into insoluble cell fractions, suggesting it is a thermosensor that allows for increased Hsf1 activity by reducing HspA8’s ability to monomerize Hsf1. During ongoing heat shock, upregulated HspA6 and HspA8 then limit the HSR presumably targeted by heat-induced DnaJB1. HspA6 knock-down and overproduction in HeLa cells suggest that HspA6 functions in preventing an overshoot of the HSR.

title: N-terminal integrity governs heptamer assembly and maturation in a mosquito innexin hemichannel
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
abstract: Nonchordate gap junction channels are formed by innexins, yet the structures and subunit assembly mechanisms of insect innexins remain unknown. We determined cryoelectron microscopy structures of AGAP001487, an innexin from the malaria mosquito Anopheles gambiae , reconstituted in lipid nanodiscs. The wild-type protein forms a rotationally symmetric heptameric hemichannel with an ordered N-terminal ring stabilized by intersubunit hydrogen bonds. Whereas deletion of a single N-terminal residue preserves channel activity, removal of two or more residues markedly impairs function. Consistent with these functional defects, the structure lacking two N-terminal residues exhibits disrupted rotational symmetry, extensive N-terminal disorder, pore collapse, and altered pore–lipid interactions. In addition, two-dimensional class averages revealed a minor population of hexameric particles, consistent with a potential assembly intermediate. Together, these structures support a stepwise assembly pathway in which intersubunit hydrogen bonding stabilizes N-terminal ring formation as a maturation step leading to a fully symmetric heptameric channel. Our findings identify N-terminal integrity as a critical determinant of oligomer maturation and channel function and provide mechanistic insight into how defined oligomeric assemblies are established in large-pore channel families.
